Record task/owner, actual PR/SHA, test/review evidence, migration and rollout state when work occurs. Preserve this ID and append corrections; never infer completion from issue closure alone. ## Current rebased contract — 2026-09-24

### Ownership

- **llamactl (this package):** the selected worker's process lifecycle for qualified infrastructure CLI execution on P2.1's executor path: worker-local process admission (per binding and per credential scope on this worker), bounded queues with expiry, drain, credential-scope keying and secret redaction, cancellation of the whole process group with SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation, and a monotonic lifecycle record. `packages/remote/src/execution/admission.ts` is worker-local process capacity, not client or tenant admission.
- **Sirius (not here):** client/tenant admission, per-account quota and shared credential-account reservation (P5.2 Sirius slice); public protocol ingress; final-response exact/semantic caching; public exposure of qualified CLI profiles, enforced by the P4.2/sirius-gateway fail-closed exposure gate once P2.2 is accepted for that profile (decision 1828 D4; there is no separate P2.2 Sirius slice).
- **Penumbra (not here):** the developer/engineer harness: coding workflows, reviews, memory, approvals, and its own CLI/ACP children and sessions. Its only involvement is the separate, evidence-only slice `P2.2/penumbra-qualification` (follow-up 1830). Full Penumbra delegation remains optional, unfiled and never on this path (D8).
- **Nova (not here):** shared contracts only: `ProviderExecutionContext`, `StreamCompletion` and `UsageObservationV1` (nova#1), and `ExecutionEventV1`, whose single definer is the P4.1 Nova slice (D5). Nova is not a home for process supervisors.
- **Embersynth:** no role. Developer orchestration (goals, agent selection, worktrees, reviews, approvals, memory, registrar) stays outside llamactl.
- **Single runtime owner:** for every execution this package admits, the selected llamactl worker is the only runtime that owns the child process group, the credential set passed to it, any permission decision, and the ephemeral, sessionless execution. Neither Penumbra nor a second worker may adopt, resume, retry or duplicate it, and llamactl never hands a queued, failed or uncertain execution to another runtime.

### Problem

The dispatch base contains P2.1 (#134). On the executor path it already delivers: an explicit child environment (a `PATH`/`HOME` baseline, the binding's allowlisted names and its resolved `env` values); a stdout cap, a bounded stderr tail and a line cap, with overflow ending in P2.1's typed overflow terminal; caller cancellation on the buffered path; one terminal per invocation; a per-invocation empty temporary working directory; and the rollout controls (`LLAMACTL_PROXY_CLI` plus per-binding enablement). P2.2 extends these and must not re-specify them. For context, at c2a6a83c the child inherits the full worker environment (`mergeEnv(opts.env ?? process.env, opts.binding.env)` at [L261](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L261), [L402](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L402) and [L480](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L480); defined at L620-L623), and nonstream `createResponse` takes no caller signal or deadline ([L529](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L529)); the nova#1 `ProviderExecutionContext`, not yet merged at the reviewed nova main 8a22acf (`@nova/contracts` 0.1.0), will supply them.

What remains after P2.1:

1. **Cancellation reaches only the direct child.** Both default spawns call a bare `proc.kill()` on abort, with no process group and no escalation ([adapter.ts L651-L773](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L651-L773)); P2.1 leaves group cleanup and escalation here. A descendant that keeps stdout open, or a child that ignores SIGTERM, holds the reader, the temporary directory and the capacity indefinitely. P2.1's overflow kill has the same gap.
2. **No admission.** Nothing bounds concurrent children per binding or per credential scope; there is no queue, expiry or drain.
3. **No credential scope or redaction.** P2.1's environment is per binding, so no cap or pool can be keyed by a scope shared across bindings. Stderr snippets enter error messages unredacted ([L207-L208](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L207-L208), [L382](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L382)), so a resolved overlay secret echoed by a CLI can reach errors and the journal.
4. **No lifecycle record.** P2.1's single terminal covers one spawn; nothing makes queue, drain, escalation and reap outcomes monotonic, or proves that no success-parseable `done` follows an `error` ([L359-L388](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L359-L388)) on those paths.

A CLI agent can have side effects. Unknown outcomes, disconnect after acceptance, and error-then-done sequences must never trigger duplicate agent work.

### Scope

1. **Worker-local admission** in `packages/remote/src/execution/admission.ts` (new):
   - Bounded concurrency and a FIFO queue per binding and per credential scope, with a queue depth limit and a queue-wait deadline. The request's absolute deadline bounds queue wait plus execution.
   - **Admission is decided before P4.1 returns `accepted`**, inside P4.1's acceptance for the `cli` backend kind and after P4.1's own fencing. A request waiting in the queue is not accepted. At dequeue, admission re-verifies the P2.1 execution-owner binding at the request's invocation revision and that the scope's secret references still resolve on this worker. Only then does a slot become held and P4.1 return `accepted`.
   - Every admission refusal is a P4.1 `rejected` result, with nothing started:

     | Local reason (journal `error_code`, occupancy) | P4.1 `rejected.code` |
     | --- | --- |
     | `queue-full`, `queue-expired`, `draining` | `overloaded` |
     | `not-owner` | `not-owner` |
     | `deadline-exceeded` | `deadline-exceeded` |
     | `credential-scope-unavailable` | `target-unavailable` |

     Local reasons are kebab-case, like the adapter journal codes ([L155-L158](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts#L155-L158)) and P4.1. They are never sent as new wire codes. A code P4.1 lacks is a blocker for the P4.1 owner, not a local extension.
   - A queued request whose caller disconnects or cancels its `cancelId` before acceptance leaves the queue and never spawns.
   - The one post-acceptance, pre-spawn case: an accepted execution holding its slot is cancelled or reaches its deadline before its child spawns. It ends as exactly one `ExecutionEventV1` terminal marked not started (P4.1 status never `started`).
   - If the accepted P4.1 seam cannot run admission before `accepted` without editing a P4.1 file, stop and report a blocker to the P4.1 owner.
   - Each slot is released exactly once on every terminal path. `drain(deadline)` rejects new and queued requests (`draining`), lets active executions run until the deadline, then cancels them through the same escalation.
2. **Process supervision** in `packages/remote/src/execution/process-supervisor.ts` (new), implementing llamactl's existing `SpawnFn`/`SpawnStreamFn` contract:
   - Spawn each child in its own process group on POSIX. Cancel with SIGTERM to the group, then SIGKILL to the group after the host-configured `cancelGraceMs`. The watchdog is the binding's `timeoutMs` or the request deadline, whichever is earlier.
   - Align with (do not import) `shutdownSignalTarget`/`gracefulShutdown` in [packages/core/src/engines/lifecycle.ts L45-L70](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3/packages/core/src/engines/lifecycle.ts#L45-L70). They are not exported from `@llamactl/core`, and `gracefulShutdown` returns once the leader exits without a group SIGKILL sweep (L62-L63). Its 10 s engine default does not become the CLI `cancelGraceMs` default.
   - At the grace deadline, SIGKILL the group whatever the leader's state. Before reporting exit, confirm the group is gone: `process.kill(-pgid, 0)` fails with ESRCH.
   - Cancel readers so a descendant holding a pipe cannot hang the consumer. Clear escalation timers on exit. Report exit only after that group check passes, and remove P2.1's temporary directory only then.
   - Pass P2.1's constructed environment verbatim; never default to `process.env`.
   - This module is the single seam that Path A may later back with a qualified library.
3. **Capture at group level.** Reuse P2.1's output-limit field, stderr tail, line cap and overflow code. P2.2 adds no capture field. Overflow and every other terminal path act on the whole group through the supervisor, and captured-byte counters are recorded. A stderr cap is added only if P2.1's merged stderr is unbounded (recorded at preflight).
4. **Credential scope and redaction:**
   - Environment construction stays P2.1's; P2.2 adds no allowlist or per-preset names. The P2.1 model-selector and tool-deny carriers (argv or environment) pass through unchanged.
   - `credentialScope` keys admission and any pool (by digest). It defaults to the binding itself; naming one scope on several bindings shares its cap.
   - Resolved overlay values are redacted from stderr snippets, error messages and journal entries.
   - P2.1's per-invocation empty temporary directory stays the only working directory. There is no workspace field.
5. **Monotonic lifecycle record** in `packages/remote/src/execution/cli-executor.ts` and `packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts`. Each accepted execution has exactly one outcome, never revised, using P2.1's merged codes (P2.2 renames none):

   | Event | Outcome |
   | --- | --- |
   | Caller or worker RPC cancel | `cancelled` |
   | Deadline or watchdog | `failed`, P2.1 `timeout` |
   | Output overflow | `failed`, P2.1 overflow code (`output-limit` in P2.1's contract) |
   | Nonzero exit | `failed`, P2.1 nonzero-exit code |
   | Cancel or deadline after acceptance, before spawn | terminal, not started |
   | Client disconnect or transport loss after acceptance (worker side) | abort through the same group escalation; P2.1 `cancelled` terminal in the worker record. The caller-visible P4.1 `status` may read `unknown` and is never a replay signal |

   - The worker-local record never holds `unknown`: the worker always knows its own child's exit.
   - After an `error`, no `done` is success-parseable; use the mapping the accepted `ExecutionEventV1` defines.
   - Nothing accepted is replayed, and a caller-side `unknown` status is never a replay signal. Cancelled worker terminals, and executions whose caller-visible status reads `unknown`, report usage `source: "unknown"` with no counts.
6. **Configuration** in `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`: an optional `lifecycle` block on `CliBindingSchema` with only `maxConcurrent`, `maxQueued`, `queueTimeoutMs`, `cancelGraceMs` and `credentialScope`, plus, if needed, one optional worker-level cap per credential scope next to the `cli` array. No second environment allowlist, output limit, workspace or mode switch.
   - **Composition rule:** P2.1's controls are the only switch. After P2.2 merges, every execution on P2.1's executor path runs under this lifecycle; an enabled binding without a `lifecycle` block gets the documented defaults, applied at execution time and never injected at parse. The in-process legacy path (controls off) is unchanged.
   - Existing configs parse to the same value. The PR records the final field names.
7. **Worker RPC gating proof:** with P2.1's controls off, P4.1's typed-unavailable refusal stays and nothing spawns. With them on in the fixture, the qualified profile runs under the lifecycle. This package edits no P4.1 file.
8. **Shared-library decision (SHAREDLIB-6), exactly one path:**
   - **Path B, D7 fallback** when follow-up 1830 is closed dropped or recorded too coupled: harden the narrow llamactl CLI path as above with no Penumbra dependency; `packages/remote/package.json` and `bun.lock` stay untouched. P6.1 stays deferred.
   - **Path B, qualification pending** when 1830 is open at preflight: stop and report dispatch blocked on qualification, unless the operator has recorded authorization to proceed on Path B pending. With that authorization, implement as the D7 fallback does, and the acceptance record labels the verdict "qualification pending" and states that llamactl adoption stays owed. That adoption is the slice `P2.2/llamactl-adoption` (see Linked repository slices).
   - Any other state of 1830 at preflight selects no path: stop and report.
   - **Path A** only if 1830 closed DONE with L1-L6 evidence and the operator recorded the library home and versioned channel. Back `process-supervisor.ts` with the packed library at the `SpawnFn`/`SpawnStreamFn` level, not Penumbra's `DispatchEvent` model. `packages/remote/package.json` and `bun.lock` join the fence only then, through a scope change recorded before any edit. llamactl injects environment, credentials, cancel grace, watchdog and any pool key. Penumbra consumer parity is proven in the qualification slice.

Preflight records the behavior on the dispatch base. If the base carries a grace constant (the P0.2 consumer lane's `CLI_KILL_GRACE_MS`, see preflight step 11, or one from P2.1), it is the default to preserve; otherwise this package chooses and records `cancelGraceMs`. No library default may set llamactl's grace or watchdog, including Penumbra's 10 s default ([cli-spawn.ts L89](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/agentchat/src/adapters/cli-spawn.ts#L89)), its `PENUMBRA_CANCEL_GRACE_S` override ([L297](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/agentchat/src/adapters/cli-spawn.ts#L297)) or any other `PENUMBRA_*` setting.

### Non-goals

- No dependency on the full Penumbra suite; Penumbra need not be installed. No dependency on its daemon, database, workflows, memory, registrar or configuration, and no read of a Penumbra home directory.
- No import of private sibling source paths, and no `file:`, `workspace:` or sibling-checkout channel for any library.
- No public gateway or protocol ingress, no final-response exact or semantic cache, and no client/tenant admission or account quota (Sirius).
- No second RPC and no new wire code: execution stays behind the single P4.1 worker RPC.
- No automatic takeover, fallback, session transfer or duplicate tool execution between runtimes, and no fallback to the legacy path, another binding or another worker.
- Package-specific exclusions:
  - no new rollout switch, environment allowlist, output limit, overflow code or workspace setting (P2.1 owns them);
  - no ACP (P6.1), sessions or resume (P6.2), placement or cross-worker retry (P5.2);
  - no usage module or physical-usage accounting (P2.1 and P1.3);
  - no model-selection, carrier or tool-policy changes (P2.1);
  - no edits to P4.1-owned files such as `packages/core/src/inference/rpc-schema.ts`, `packages/remote/src/inference/procedures.ts`, `packages/remote/src/inference/client.ts` or the tunnel modules;
  - no qualification work in the Penumbra repository, and no enabling of any binding or profile.

- A read-only occupancy snapshot (active, queued, draining per binding and credential scope) for health and placement. It is not an account quota; the historical "shared-account quota seam for fleet reservations" moves to Sirius (P5.2).

### Test strategy

BOUNDARY task class: tests come first. Fixtures use real fake executables; do not mock `Bun.spawn` in new tests. No production inference, no real credentials. Process-group cases and acceptance run on POSIX; a skip never counts as a pass.

1. **Round trip first (RED): `packages/remote/test/cli-lifecycle-roundtrip.test.ts`.** Drive the producer (the accepted P4.1 embedded worker RPC client, the P2.1 executor with its controls on, the fake executable) and assert only through consumer schemas and OS state: every event parses with the pinned Nova `ExecutionEventV1`; every submit result parses with P4.1's `InferenceRpcV1` schema; liveness uses `process.kill(pid, 0)`. Cases:
   - (a) `fork-descendant` streaming, cancel through the worker RPC after the first chunk: one `cancelled` terminal, no success-parseable `done`; parent and descendant gone (ESRCH) within `cancelGraceMs` plus a scheduler allowance; occupancy back to zero; a waiting request then admitted.
   - (b) Nonstream, near `ProviderExecutionContext.deadline`: `failed` with P2.1 `timeout`, group reaped.
   - (c) `error-then-exit`: `failed`, no success-parseable `done`.
   - (d) Overflow at admission (`maxConcurrent` 1, `maxQueued` 0, one execution running): the second submit is `rejected` with `overloaded`, the journal records `queue-full`, and the fake CLI's invocation count stays at one.
   - (e) P2.1 controls off: P4.1 refuses with typed `target-unavailable`, zero invocations.
   - (f) Disconnect after acceptance over the P4.1 client, once before the first event and once mid-stream: the group is reaped (ESRCH within `cancelGraceMs` plus the allowance), the worker records exactly one `cancelled` terminal, the fake CLI's invocation count stays at one, and nothing is replayed.
   - Run on the dispatch base before implementing and record that it fails for the contract gap (descendant survives, no admission rejection), not a compile or fixture error. Then GREEN; then a deliberate mutation (drop SIGKILL escalation, signal only the direct child, or return on leader exit) shown failing; restore and re-run.
2. **Admission: `execution-admission.test.ts`.** Queue overflow (`queue-full` -> `overloaded`) and expiry (`queue-expired` -> `overloaded`) with no spawn; a per-scope cap across two bindings sharing a scope; ownership revoked while queued (`not-owner`) and unresolvable scope secrets (`credential-scope-unavailable` -> `target-unavailable`) at dequeue, before `accepted`; caller disconnect and `cancelId` cancel while queued remove the entry; cancel after acceptance but before spawn gives one not-started terminal; drain; each slot released exactly once on success, failure, cancel, overflow and missing-binary spawn failure. Count fake-CLI invocations to prove "no spawn".
3. **Supervisor: `cli-process-supervisor.test.ts`.** A child ignoring SIGTERM gets SIGKILL after the grace; in `fork-term-resistant-descendant` mode the descendant is ESRCH within `cancelGraceMs` plus the allowance after its leader exits; an early consumer return and P2.1 overflow both terminate the whole group; readers do not hang on a descendant-held pipe; no timer remains after reap; the temporary directory is removed only after reap; caller abort gives `cancelled`, deadline gives `timeout`; an overlay secret echoed on stderr never appears in errors or the journal; a `PENUMBRA_CANCEL_GRACE_S` value has no effect. **Carrier non-regression (X1, X6):** for each built-in preset under the lifecycle path, the `env-dump` and argv logs show P2.1's model-selector and tool-deny carriers present and identical to P2.1's executor spawn, the environment equals P2.1's construction, and bypass-flag rejection still holds.
4. **Installation: `cli-lifecycle-install.test.ts`.** I1-I6 below, with temporary runtimes following `makeTempRuntime`/`envForTemp` in `packages/core/test/helpers.ts` (re-created in the test subtree if not importable). Dependency closure: under Path B, no `@penumbra/` specifier or import in `packages/remote`; under Path A, exactly one versioned library dependency and no `file:`, `workspace:` or git-sibling specifier.
5. **Upgrade: extend `cli-schema.test.ts`.** Pre-change bindings, including P2.1-era enabled bindings, parse to the same value; an absent `lifecycle` stays absent after parse, and the executor applies the documented defaults at run time.
6. **Fixture `fake-cli-lifecycle.ts`:** a bun-shebang executable copied into a temporary directory per test; modes `echo`, `stream-lines`, `hang`, `fork-descendant`, `term-resistant`, `fork-term-resistant-descendant` (the leader exits on SIGTERM; a descendant ignores SIGTERM and holds stdout), `no-newline-flood`, `stderr-flood`, `partial-then-nonzero`, `error-then-exit`, `echo-secret` and `env-dump`.

`cli-adapter.test.ts`, `cli-stream.test.ts` and P2.1's suites are regression checks and pass unmodified.

### Acceptance criteria

EXEC-7:

- **X1 model-selection enforcement:** P2.1 owns it. Non-regression: under the lifecycle every spawn carries P2.1's selector carrier unchanged (Test 3).
- **X2 worker ownership verified before spawn:** at dequeue, before `accepted` and before spawn, admission re-verifies the execution-owner binding at the invocation revision and the credential scope. Failure is a P4.1 `rejected` (`not-owner` or `target-unavailable`) and no process is created.
- **X3 bounded streaming and capture:** P2.1's caps hold under the lifecycle; overflow terminates the whole group with P2.1's overflow code; counters show nothing past the caps; queues are bounded by `maxQueued`.
- **X4 cancellation end to end:** caller abort, `cancelId` and worker RPC cancel reach queued, accepted-not-spawned and running executions; the whole group, including pipe-holding descendants and SIGTERM-resistant children, is gone within `cancelGraceMs` plus the allowance; in `fork-term-resistant-descendant` mode the descendant is ESRCH within `cancelGraceMs` plus the allowance after its leader exits; readers cancelled; slot released once; `cancelled` distinct from `timeout`. Disconnect after acceptance (round-trip case (f)) reaps the group with exactly one `cancelled` worker terminal, one invocation and no replay.
- **X5 credential isolation:** the supervisor passes P2.1's environment verbatim and never `process.env`; admission and any pool are keyed by credential scope; overlay values are redacted from captured, journaled and error text.
- **X6 tool permissions (deny by default):** P2.1 owns deny-by-default through the verified per-preset tool-deny carrier. Non-regression: under the lifecycle every spawn still carries the carrier in argv or environment, and bypass-flag rejection still holds (Test 3). ACP permissions are P6.1.
- **X7 session fencing:** N/A; executions are ephemeral, and sessions are P6.2 with P5.1 fencing. Non-regression: admission neither accepts nor persists a session identifier.

Outcomes and records:

- Every admission refusal is a P4.1 `rejected` code per the Scope 1 table, with zero fake-CLI invocations. Each accepted execution has exactly one monotonic terminal; an error is never followed by a success-parseable `done`; the worker-local record never holds `unknown`; nothing accepted is replayed and a caller-side `unknown` status is never a replay signal; cancelled worker terminals and executions whose caller-visible status reads `unknown` carry usage `source: "unknown"` without counts.
- Historical criteria retained: cancellation or timeout releases slots and process resources within the bound; output never accumulates without bound; CLI fixtures pass for JSON and SSE through the worker RPC; owner accounting is single-writer.
- The acceptance record names each qualified CLI profile and states the SHAREDLIB-6 path.

INSTALL-6:

- **I1 clean install:** with Penumbra not installed, a clean llamactl install at the recorded baseline serves an enabled CLI binding under the lifecycle against the fake CLI. Path B adds no dependency and leaves `bun.lock` unchanged; Path A adds exactly one versioned library.
- **I2 existing-config upgrade:** existing `cli` bindings parse unchanged; the legacy path is unchanged with P2.1's controls off; `cli-adapter.test.ts` and `cli-stream.test.ts` pass unmodified.
- **I3 optional service absent:** with Penumbra, Sirius and Embersynth absent and unconfigured, worker startup and health are unaffected; nothing probes or imports them.
- **I4 selected integration unavailable:** an enabled binding whose scope secrets do not resolve, whose executable is missing, or (Path A) whose library is missing fails closed as typed unavailable, with no fallback to the legacy path, another binding, another worker or Penumbra.
- **I5 disconnect and rollback:** turning off either P2.1 control refuses new requests, rejects queued ones before acceptance and drains active executions within the bound; reverting the commit restores P2.1 behavior; a reverted build loads configs containing `lifecycle` (inferred from the non-strict schema; the fixture confirms); no standalone setting or credential is lost.
- **I6 nothing new required:** diff commands, services, config fields and credential entries against the follow-up 1832 baseline; every new field is optional; no second switch, allowlist or output limit; credentials remain the host CLI login plus existing secret references; the grandfathered `../nova` dependency is not extended. No new mandatory service, setup entry point, sibling checkout or duplicate provider/credential entry; the D12 duplication baseline does not increase; existing setup entry points and compatible configuration are reused.

SHAREDLIB-6 (mandatory):

- **Path B, D7 fallback:** L1-L5 recorded as not adopted, with evidence (no new dependency, no `@penumbra/` import, the cited 1830 status: dropped or too coupled). L6 proven. P6.1 stays deferred.
- **Path B, qualification pending** (only with recorded operator authorization): the same evidence as the D7 fallback, plus the cited authorization. The acceptance record labels the verdict "qualification pending" and states that llamactl adoption stays owed as `P2.2/llamactl-adoption`, recorded in the manifest `slices[]`.
- **Path A:** cite the qualification slice's L1 closure counts, L3 Penumbra parity and L5 release. Prove here: L2 install from the packed tarball through the chosen channel with no Penumbra checkout, daemon, database, memory or extra configuration; L3 fake CLI fixtures pass against the packed artifact; L4 llamactl injects environment, credentials, selectors, workspace, cancel grace and watchdog, with library defaults and `PENUMBRA_*` settings having no effect and pool keys including a credential-scope digest; L6.
- **L6, either path:** exactly one selected runtime owns each process, credential set, permission decision and execution; no automatic takeover, unsafe fallback or duplicate tool execution between llamactl and Penumbra.

### Rollout and rollback

- No new switch: P2.1's `LLAMACTL_PROXY_CLI` and per-binding enablement, both default off, stay the only enablement, and this package enables nothing. Lifecycle defaults are conservative.
- Canary: one explicitly enabled binding with one credential scope; caching and automatic retries stay disabled.
- Rollback: turn off either P2.1 control. New admissions are refused, queued requests are rejected before acceptance, and active executions drain within the bound, then are cancelled through the same escalation. Only process groups this worker created are signalled. Reverting the commit restores P2.1 behavior; Path A reverts to the Path B supervisor with no configuration change.
- No automatic takeover: nothing moves to another runtime, worker or binding on rollback, drain or failure.

### Fleet execution contract v2

- **Task:** task_class **BOUNDARY**, task_type **implement_substantial**, stable ID **P2.2**, slice `P2.2/llamactl`, issue https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/135.
- **Repository:** frozename/llamactl, verified with `git remote get-url origin` before any write; isolated worktree; one writer per overlapping fence.
- **Branch:** `feat/ai-router-p2-2-cli-lifecycle` (naming convention only; seats are resolved at dispatch).
- **Base:** llamactl main after P0.2 acceptance, containing the accepted P4.1 and P2.1 merges. Reviewed at c2a6a83c4bcbe36ff7651b7ca6d675068e2103a3.
- **Preflight** (stop on any failure):
  1. Verify origin, fetch main, record base SHA and clean status, read AGENTS.md.
  2. Confirm P0.2 (#130), P4.1 (#139) and P2.1 (#134) are accepted, with merged PR SHAs on main; issue closure is not enough.
  3. Re-verify every fence and focused-check path on the dispatch base; `cli-executor.ts` must exist. Confirm no open lane holds `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`, `packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts` or `packages/remote/test/cli-schema.test.ts`.
  4. Record the merged P2.1 `CliBindingSchema` fields, typed codes (overflow, timeout, nonzero exit, rejections), stderr bound and enablement controls; reuse them, and record any rename as a scope change.
  5. Record where P4.1's `cli` seam decides acceptance and confirm admission can run before `accepted` without a P4.1 edit; otherwise stop with a blocker for the P4.1 owner.
  6. Pin Nova to the nova main commit containing merged nova#1 (contracts 0.2.0; reviewed main 8a22acf still has 0.1.0); run `bun install` in each consumer after any Nova change.
  7. Record the shared-library path from the latest state of follow-up 1830 by Scope 8's rule: Path A; Path B, D7 fallback; or, if 1830 is open, stop blocked on qualification unless the operator has recorded authorization for Path B, qualification pending.
  8. Record the cancellation behavior on the base (grace constant or none).
  9. Capture the baseline of every required gate: pass/fail/skip counts and failing test names.
  10. Record the installation baseline on the dispatch base per follow-up 1832: required commands and the existing setup entry point, services, config fields and credential entries, the grandfathered `../nova` `file:` dependency, and the D12 duplication baseline (llamactl `cli[]` versus Penumbra `agents.yaml`). I1 and I6 diff against this record.
  11. The merged P0.2 consumer lane (registrar 1839; head `ce019e9f`) already added SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation (`CLI_KILL_GRACE_MS`) and drain-to-EOF truncation reporting in `packages/remote/src/cli/adapter.ts`. Confirm both are on the base and record where they live. P2.2's supervisor extends that escalation to the process group rather than duplicating it, and must not regress either behavior.
- **Required gates** at the llamactl root: `bun run typecheck`; `bun run lint`; `bun test`; `zsh test/run-all.zsh`; `git diff --exit-code <base> HEAD -- packages/remote/test/cli-adapter.test.ts packages/remote/test/cli-stream.test.ts`. Cross-repository consumer gates (AGENTS.md): `bun test` in verified nova, sirius-gateway and embersynth worktrees; a missing checkout is a gap, never a pass. Path A adds the Penumbra package gates, the qualification slice's agentchat parity evidence and a packed-tarball install check without a Penumbra checkout.
- **Focused checks** (cwd `packages/remote`; a new file matching zero tests is a failure): `bun test test/cli-lifecycle-roundtrip.test.ts` (new); `bun test test/execution-admission.test.ts` (new); `bun test test/cli-process-supervisor.test.ts` (new); `bun test test/cli-lifecycle-install.test.ts` (new); `bun test test/cli-schema.test.ts`; regression `bun test test/cli-adapter.test.ts` and `bun test test/cli-stream.test.ts`.
- **Discipline:** RED round trip failing for the contract gap, GREEN, a deliberate mutation shown failing, restoration, then fresh focused and full gates. Record command, cwd, exit code, counts, mutation proof and final SHA.
- **Review:** independent adversarial review at the final SHA by a different seat than the implementer; the implementer's summary is not enough.
- **Return:** VERDICT PASS or FAIL; issue URL; base and final SHAs; fence proof; RED/GREEN/mutation evidence; EXEC-7, INSTALL-6 and SHAREDLIB-6 evidence; qualified CLI profiles and rollback evidence; review verdict, unresolved findings and PR URL. No merge, deployment, live credentials, live model runs or feature enablement.

The historical record below is unchanged except for marked annotations and status lines. It is not part of the dispatched task.
task_file.acceptance_criteria: Implement the P2.2 current rebased contract (fleet v2, decision 1828, slice P2.2/llamactl) on P2.1's executor path only, extending P2.1 without re-specifying it: reuse P2.1's environment construction, output-limit field, stderr tail, line cap, overflow code, per-invocation temporary directory and rollout controls (the only enablement switch; an enabled binding without a lifecycle block gets documented defaults). Add worker-local admission with bounded per-binding and per-credential-scope queues, expiry and drain, decided before P4.1 returns accepted (including dequeue-time owner and credential-scope re-verification), with every refusal expressed as a P4.1 rejected code (queue-full/queue-expired/draining -> overloaded, not-owner -> not-owner, deadline-exceeded -> deadline-exceeded, credential-scope-unavailable -> target-unavailable; local kebab-case reasons only in the journal and occupancy snapshot) and zero spawns; one not-started ExecutionEventV1 terminal for cancel or deadline after acceptance but before spawn; process-group supervision with SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation at a host-configured cancelGraceMs (aligned with, not imported from, core engines/lifecycle.ts, whose 10 s default is not inherited), SIGKILL to the group at the grace deadline whatever the leader's state, and exit reported only after process.kill(-pgid, 0) fails with ESRCH (proven with the fork-term-resistant-descendant fixture mode, with return-on-leader-exit as an accepted mutation), building on the P0.2 consumer lane's escalation and drain-to-EOF truncation reporting in adapter.ts without duplicating or regressing them; credential-scope keying and overlay-secret redaction; exactly one monotonic terminal per accepted execution with no success-parseable done after error and no automatic replay; client disconnect or transport loss after acceptance aborts through the same group escalation and ends in one worker-side P2.1 cancelled terminal (the worker record never holds unknown; the caller-visible P4.1 status may read unknown and is never a replay signal), proven by round-trip case (f) before the first event and mid-stream. Optional lifecycle fields only: maxConcurrent, maxQueued, queueTimeoutMs, cancelGraceMs, credentialScope. Prove EXEC-7 X2-X5, X1 and X6 non-regression (P2.1 model-selector and tool-deny carriers preserved in argv/environment for each built-in preset; bypass-flag rejection holds), X7 non-regression, INSTALL-6 I1-I6 against the installation baseline recorded at preflight per follow-up 1832 (no new mandatory service, setup entry point, sibling checkout or duplicate provider/credential entry; the D12 duplication baseline does not increase) and SHAREDLIB-6 on the recorded path (Path A only if follow-up 1830 closed DONE and the operator chose home and channel; Path B, D7 fallback if 1830 was dropped or recorded too coupled; if 1830 is open, stop blocked on qualification unless the operator recorded authorization for Path B, qualification pending, in which case the verdict is labelled 'qualification pending' and llamactl adoption stays owed as slice P2.2/llamactl-adoption), with a RED-first producer-consumer round trip through the P4.1 worker RPC parsed with the pinned Nova ExecutionEventV1 and P4.1 InferenceRpcV1 schemas (including an overloaded rejection with zero fake-CLI invocations), mutation proof, cli-adapter and cli-stream suites unmodified, all required gates green against a recorded baseline, and independent review by a different seat. Name each qualified CLI profile and the shared-library verdict; public exposure of a qualified CLI profile is enforced by the P4.2/sirius-gateway fail-closed exposure gate once P2.2 is accepted for that profile (no separate P2.2 Sirius slice). No Penumbra suite dependency, no private sibling source imports, no P4.1 file edits, no merge, deployment or feature enablement.

issues.title: [AI router P3.1] Define semantic-cache safety, identity and calibration profiles
issues.body:
## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 3 — Semantic cache
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/133.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

Temperature zero or an exact request fingerprint does not justify approximate reuse. Semantic hits must be explicitly opted into, strictly scoped and evaluated before any response is served.

## Scope

1. Implement eligibility before embedding: initial single-turn text QA only. Bypass tools, structured output, seed/reproducibility profiles, CLI/ACP, sessions, multimodal, RAG and unsupported generation controls.
2. Define compatibility scope over authenticated tenant/account, public model and immutable generation/config revision, protocolVariant, system/policy fingerprint, generation parameters, embedding model/version/dimension and representation version.
3. Canonicalize only the eligible semantic text; hash all safety-relevant exact fields into the namespace. Do not truncate over-limit content or embed secrets silently. Keep Anthropic, Chat and Responses semantic caches isolated.
4. Build labeled paraphrases and hard negatives for numbers, negation, locale, system instructions and domain constraints. Record per-profile score threshold, TTL and maximum acceptable false-hit rate; a similarity score is not a correctness proof.

## Concrete file/module targets

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

- `packages/core/src/semanticcache/eligibility.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/semanticcache/identity.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/semanticcache/types.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`
- `packages/core/src/cache-identity/canonical.ts` (preserve V1)
- `packages/core/test/semanticcache/fixtures/` (new)

## Contracts and schemas

CacheScopeV2 and SemanticCachePolicySchema with off|shadow|serve, allowlisted profile, cosine threshold, absolute TTL, embedder revision, limits and provenance. Distinct exact/semantic identities.

## Test strategy

Add packages/core/test/semanticcache/eligibility.test.ts and identity.test.ts. Test same text under different tenants, credential accounts, model/config/system/protocol scopes; all disallowed features; Unicode and length limits; old exact canonical keys remain unchanged.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. Run focused tests and required typecheck/lint plus the AGENTS.md four-repository gate (llamactl, nova, sirius-gateway, embersynth) for implementation slices. Report unavailable sibling checkouts as gaps. No production inference/credentials in hermetic CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Eligibility and strict namespace checks run before any embedding call.
- [ ] All protocol variants are isolated, and unsupported/side-effect profiles bypass approximate cache.
- [ ] Calibration dataset and decision fields are present; no default claim that a threshold is universally safe.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

LLAMACTL_SEMANTIC_CACHE defaults off. Ship policy and shadow instrumentation independently of serving. No migration or sensitive-prompt backfill.

## Verified baseline references

Baseline: frozename/llamactl@7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb. The implementation acceptance tests listed above are planned, not claimed as implemented or passing. Reference inspection is complete in R0.

- **S15 — Cache identity, eligibility, persistence and eviction:** [packages/core/src/cache-identity/canonical.ts: 1–53](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/cache-identity/canonical.ts#L1-L53); [packages/core/src/responsecache/deterministic.ts: 1–11](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/responsecache/deterministic.ts#L1-L11); [packages/core/src/responsecache/registry.ts: 3–118](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/responsecache/registry.ts#L3-L118); [packages/core/src/responsecache/storage.ts: 1–170](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/responsecache/storage.ts#L1-L170); [packages/core/src/responsecache/policy.ts: 1–76](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/responsecache/policy.ts#L1-L76); [packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts: 798–989](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts#L798-L989).

- **S16 — Epoch scoping, oMLX handling and KV locality:** [packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts: 753–829](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts#L753-L829); [packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts: 904–989](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts#L904-L989); [packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts: 1175–1272](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts#L1175-L1272); [packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts: 1399–1440](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts#L1399-L1440); [packages/core/src/kvstore/workloadEpoch.ts: 1–57](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/src/kvstore/workloadEpoch.ts#L1-L57).

- **S18 — Exact-cache and peer-epoch integration assertions:** [packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts: 189–344](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts#L189-L344); [packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts: 435–686](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts#L435-L686); [packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts: 962–1159](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts#L962-L1159); [packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts: 1160–1508](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/core/test/responsecache/proxy-integration.test.ts#L1160-L1508).

- **S25 — Embedding reuse and pgvector limits of current RAG adapter:** [packages/remote/src/rag/embedding.ts: 23–87](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/remote/src/rag/embedding.ts#L23-L87); [packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/adapter.ts: 146–205](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/adapter.ts#L146-L205); [packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/adapter.ts: 368–403](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/adapter.ts#L368-L403); [packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/client.ts: 16–101](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb/packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/client.ts#L16-L101).

## Execution and review discipline

Task class: BOUNDARY (producer-consumer round-trip first, then independent review). Revalidate the named file fence against current main before implementation. Shared schema/proxy edits have one owner at a time. Use the focused bun:test paths above, then `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun test` in llamactl, Nova, sirius-gateway and embersynth. issues.title: [AI router P3.2] Add pgvector response-cache storage and validated embedding
issues.body:
## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 3 — Semantic cache
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/136.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

Existing RAG embedding and pgvector plumbing can be reused, but RAG search lacks the response-cache scope/TTL and atomic complete-payload guarantees. A semantic result must not point to a lost SQLite payload on another node.

## Scope

1. Choose optional pgvector with HNSW for fleet-ready semantic storage; keep local exact-only SQLite deployments independent of Postgres. Reuse embedder bindings and SQL client, not the RAG adapter's document contract.
2. Create dedicated complete response/vector records with immutable scope/revisions, payload, completion proof, original expiry, embedding version/dimension, cost/size/provenance and indexes. Commit vector and payload atomically.
3. Implement cosine candidates with mandatory namespace/TTL filters and exact metadata/revision recheck. Validate pgvector version, dimension/index type limits, filtered ANN recall and candidate exhaustion; enable iterative scans or bounded exact fallback deliberately.
4. Wrap embedding with deadline/cancel, dimensional/finite/nonzero-norm validation, memoization and recursion/cache bypass. Fail open to upstream on cache/embedding failure within budget, without weakening tenant auth.

## Concrete file/module targets

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

- `packages/remote/src/cache/pgvector-store.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/cache/embedding.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/cache/migrations/001-response-semantic-cache.sql` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/rag/embedding.ts` (reuse/extend)
- `packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/client.ts` (reuse)
- `packages/remote/src/rag/pgvector/adapter.ts` (leave RAG responsibility separate)

## Contracts and schemas

Dedicated response payload/vector tables per design §5.4; pgvector extension/index/version checks, TTL and model-generation scope. No change to existing SQLite key interpretation.

## Test strategy

Add packages/remote/test/semantic-cache-pgvector.test.ts and semantic-cache-migration.test.ts against real disposable PG/pgvector. Test HNSW vs exact-distance recall, selective tenant filters, vector validation, schema upgrades/restart, concurrent write rollback, expired records, missing payload prevention and outage timeout.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. Run focused tests and required typecheck/lint plus the AGENTS.md four-repository gate (llamactl, nova, sirius-gateway, embersynth) for implementation slices. Report unavailable sibling checkouts as gaps. No production inference/credentials in hermetic CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every hit has an atomically stored complete payload and matching strict scope.
- [ ] Indexes work with the selected embedder dimension/version and restrictive filters; metadata is rechecked.
- [ ] Embedding/cache outage falls through without recursion or excessive added latency.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

Optional PG migration; no automatic backfill. Shadow-only first. Disabling semantic cache leaves SQLite exact behavior intact.

## Verified baseline references

issues.body:
## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 3 — Semantic cache
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/137.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

The semantic tier must save work without adding embedding cost on exact hits, leaking scopes, extending old answers indefinitely or publishing partial streams.

## Scope

1. Wire exact lookup first, eligibility second, semantic lookup third and upstream last. Preserve worker-local KV only beneath upstream execution. Recheck scope/generation at lookup, publication and serve.
2. Publish only completed successful upstream answers. Promote semantic hits to exact only with provenance and original absolute expiry; never create semantic-from-semantic chains or slide TTL.
3. Extend responsecache/policy.ts scoring to include byte/vector quota, recency, frequency, actual avoided cost and age; hard-delete expired/revoked entries before scoring. Add bounded maintenance and per-tenant/model quotas.
4. Expose hit/miss/bypass, embedding/ANN latency and cost, avoided generation cost, false-hit evaluation, bytes/evictions and model revision. Shadow mode never changes answers or duplicates billable inference without a separately budgeted evaluation policy.
5. Require recorded per-profile safety/cost/latency approval before serve mode; rollback must be a single policy change.

## Concrete file/module targets

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

- `packages/remote/src/cache/semantic-service.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/semanticcache/policy.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/cache/maintenance.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/responsecache/policy.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/proxy/create-proxy.ts`
- `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`

## Contracts and schemas

Semantic lookup/write outcomes, originalExpiresAt and provenance, eviction accounting, per-profile serving approval and revision fences.

## Test strategy

Add packages/remote/test/semantic-cache-proxy.test.ts and packages/core/test/semanticcache/policy.test.ts. Assert exact hit makes zero embedder/upstream calls; semantic paraphrase hits and hard-negative misses; scope isolation; abort/truncated stream non-publication; expiry after promotion; concurrent model swap; cache outage; eviction quota fairness.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. Run focused tests and required typecheck/lint plus the AGENTS.md four-repository gate (llamactl, nova, sirius-gateway, embersynth) for implementation slices. Report unavailable sibling checkouts as gaps. No production inference/credentials in hermetic CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three protocol scopes follow exact→semantic→upstream with no cross-protocol reuse.
- [ ] No answer survives its original TTL or changed model/policy generation.
- [ ] Serve mode remains gated until measured false-hit, recall, added latency and saved-cost criteria are recorded for each profile.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

LLAMACTL_SEMANTIC_CACHE=off|shadow|serve, allowlisted per profile. Off preserves exact cache and makes semantic records inert; no destructive downgrade.

The semantic tier must save work without adding embedding cost on exact hits, leaking scopes, extending old answers indefinitely or publishing partial streams.

## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 4 — Separation
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/135, https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/138.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

Independent proxy replicas require a stable worker execution contract. Existing tunnels provide stream/cancel primitives, but public peer forwarding is not equivalent to explicit owner RPC and some transport queues remain unbounded.

## Scope

1. Expand the Phase 2 seam into negotiated versioned catalog, execute, cancel and status contracts with accepted/unknown-outcome semantics, deadlines, route/model generations, tenant claims, attempt IDs and feature requirements.

### Problem

Sirius, the full inference gateway, and llamactl's opt-in unified proxy both need a stable, versioned contract for executing on a llamactl model worker. The unified proxy comes from P0.2, behind `LLAMACTL_UNIFIED_PROXY`, which defaults to off. Four gaps stand in the way today:

1. **The Sirius bridge has no execution contract.** Sirius reaches llamactl through the legacy `libs/provider-llamactl` bridge on the agent's OpenAI-compatible `/v1` surface (sirius-gateway 1ae980b, `libs/provider-llamactl/src/llamactl.adapter.ts`). It has no acceptance fencing, no status or unknown outcome and no cancellation acknowledgement, and it drops tools and capabilities.
2. **The `worker-rpc` transport has no dedicated executor.** At #150 head 07fdf841, P0.2 declares route transport `worker-rpc`, but the default legacy executor claims that transport and delegates to `openaiProxy.proxyOpenAI`; there is no dedicated worker-RPC executor. Re-verify on the post-P0.2 base at preflight.
3. **The tunnel buffer is unbounded.** The tunnel subscription bridge buffers values in an unbounded array (`packages/remote/src/tunnel/router-bridge.ts:278-307` at c2a6a83c), so a slow consumer grows memory without limit.
4. **Direct dials to agent nodes skip certificate pinning.** `packages/remote/src/router.ts:1256` calls `providerForNode` without a `fetchFactory`, so `packages/remote/src/providers/factory.ts:231` dials with unpinned global fetch. ### Scope

1. **Establish `InferenceRpcV1` on the P0.2 seam.** Do not redesign P0.2. The RPC provides:
   - negotiated versions and required/optional features;
   - a catalog of fixed deployments with deployment epoch and catalog generation;
   - submit, keyed by (requestId, attemptId), carrying an absolute deadline, a serialized cancellation ID, tenant/project/credential-scope claims and hop state;
   - an accepted or rejected acceptance result;
   - status (`unknown | accepted | started | emitting | terminal`);
   - cancel with an acknowledged outcome.

   Unknown required features and incompatible major versions fail closed.
2. **Fence acceptance on the worker.** Before any engine request, process start or credential acquisition, verify in this order:
   1. the service claims authorize the operation, deployment and tenant;
   2. the worker owns the deployment at the expected epoch and incarnation;
   3. the deadline has not passed;
   4. the hop count and visited-node chain (P0.2 `InternalSelectionV1`) allow execution;
   5. the backend kind is registered.

   Execute the fixed deployment directly and never re-enter public model routing. A duplicate submit with the same attemptId returns the existing record and never starts a second execution.
3. **Clients with identical semantics.**
   - Three clients: embedded (in-process, for the local node); direct (TLS-pinned HTTPS to the declared owner's endpoint through the existing `makePinnedFetch` in `packages/remote/src/client/links.ts`); and reverse tunnel (the node's `tunnelNodeName`/`tunnelPreferred`).
   - The declared owner in the kubeconfig node selects the transport. There is no probing fallback.
   - The remote client implements the P0.2 `BackendExecutor` (`describe`, `execute`, `cancel`, `drain`, `close`). The shared unified proxy acquires it for `worker-rpc` candidates only.
4. **Service claims.**
   - A worker-side binding maps a service credential, stored only as a hash, to allowed operations, deployments or models, and tenants.
   - `auth.ts` validates it. `serve.ts` and the tunnel path pass the verified claims into the RPC context.
   - The existing operator bearer keeps its current scope.
   - The envelope tenant must fall inside the presented claims.
5. **Bounded streaming.**
   - Cap frame bytes, per-stream queued bytes and slow-consumer buffers in `messages.ts`, `router-bridge.ts` and `tunnel-server.ts`.
   - On overflow, end the stream with a typed terminal error and cancel upstream. Never drop frames silently.
   - Propagate cancellation, acceptance, terminal errors and completion across tunnel reconnects.
   - Never retry automatically after output or uncertain acceptance. A timed-out submit is resolved through status, and `unknown` is surfaced to the caller rather than replayed.
6. **Return typed refusals for non-model targets.**

### Contracts and schemas

- **Consumed from P0.2, not redefined:**
  - `InferenceEnvelopeV1`;
  - `InternalSelectionV1` (`hopCount`, `visitedNodes`, `deploymentId`, `expectedDeploymentEpoch`, `catalogVersion`, `membershipEpoch`);
  - `SessionReferenceV1` (refused here);
  - `CachePolicyV1` (`semantic` must be `off`);
  - the `BackendExecutor` seam and route transport `worker-rpc`;
  - backend kinds `local-model | cloud-api | cli | acp`;
  - the Nova 0.2.0 usage and stream contracts.
- **Consumed from P4.1/nova: `ExecutionEventV1`.**
  - One acceptance event comes before any content, and the sequence is monotonic.
  - There is exactly one terminal event, carrying source-completion proof or a typed error.
  - Usage is reported as observed or as unknown.
  - llamactl validates events with the Nova schema. It defines no copy: `git grep -n -E "ExecutionEventV1Schema\s*=" -- packages` returns nothing in llamactl.
- **Defined here: `InferenceRpcV1`** in `packages/core/src/inference/rpc-schema.ts`.
  - `negotiate`: {versions, requiredFeatures, optionalFeatures} → {version, workerId, workerIncarnation, features}, or typed `unsupported-version`/`unsupported-feature`.
  - `catalog`: fixed deployments {deploymentId, model, backendKind, deploymentEpoch, catalogGeneration, availability}.
  - `submit`: {version, envelope, target {deploymentId, expectedDeploymentEpoch, catalogGeneration}, cancelId}. It returns either `accepted` {attemptId, workerIncarnation, acceptedAt}, followed by the `ExecutionEventV1` stream, or `rejected` {code: `unauthorized-scope | not-owner | stale-generation | deadline-exceeded | hop-limit | target-unavailable | unsupported-feature | unsupported-version | overloaded`}.
  - `status`: attemptId → `unknown | accepted | started | emitting | terminal`. `unknown` never means that a retry is safe.
  - `cancel`: attemptId or cancelId → an acknowledged outcome `cancelled | already-terminal | unknown`.
  - Field names are implementation contracts; the semantics above are fixed by this issue.
- **Service authorization claims:** {serviceId, operations, deployments or models, tenants, credentialScopeId}. They are bound to a hashed credential on the worker, derived server-side and never read from client headers.
- **Tunnel frames:**
  - a maximum frame size in bytes;
  - a per-stream queued-byte cap;
  - cancel and cancel-acknowledge frames;
  - terminal propagation across reconnect.
- **Rollout control:** the worker RPC negotiated version (boundaries §7) replaces `LLAMACTL_PROXY_EXECUTION`.

### Rollout and rollback

- **No new environment flag.** Two opt-ins, both off by default: a worker advertises `InferenceRpcV1` only when its agent config lists the version (an absent field means not advertised, today's behavior), and callers use the RPC only through the P0.2 unified proxy (`LLAMACTL_UNIFIED_PROXY`, off by default) after negotiation selects version 1. Direct local clients (`/v1` through `openaiProxy.ts`) are unaffected.
- **Order of enablement:** workers, then llamactl callers, then the Sirius slice.
- **Negotiation outcomes.** A negotiation that positively reports no RPC support keeps new requests on the existing path. A negotiation error or timeout fails closed with a typed unavailable result; it never falls back silently. The transport is chosen before submission and recorded for each attempt.
- **Rollback** (stop the advertisement or turn the flag off) affects new requests only. Active RPC streams drain to their terminal event or end with an acknowledged cancel. There is no automatic takeover: accepted attempts are never re-submitted through the old path, and neither a draining worker nor a caller moves one to another worker or runtime. Config fields are additive and optional, so the base release still parses them; there is no data migration.
- **The pinned-fetch default in `factory.ts`** is a defect fix with no flag; its rollback is a revert of that commit.

## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 4 — Separation
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/139.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

Moving a file alone does not separate scaling. HTTP/stream orchestration must leave core while workload lifecycle, process spawning, credentials and llama.cpp/oMLX KV ownership stay on workers.

## Scope

1. Create packages/proxy as a thin Bun composition root using remote transport/adapters and core pure contracts. Add configuration, readiness, bounded drain, catalog subscription and service identity.
2. Move orchestration from core/openaiProxy.ts into remote/proxy/handler.ts and supporting modules; preserve pure translators/policy in core. Move local-model transport and KV session orchestration to worker execution modules.
3. Atomically migrate all actual imports, server mounts, tRPC entrypoints, package exports and root build scripts; remove core/openaiProxy.ts after callers move. Do not create a permanent core→remote compatibility shim.
4. Run proxy-only processes with no runtime-directory or spawn requirement; retain embedded mode through the same handler/executor interfaces. Workers continue lifecycle/control operations independently.
5. Move transport tests to remote while preserving assertions and existing local/peer/oMLX behavior.

## Concrete file/module targets

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

- `packages/proxy/package.json` (new)
- `packages/proxy/tsconfig.json` (new)
- `packages/proxy/src/main.ts` (new)
- `packages/proxy/src/config.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/proxy/handler.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/proxy/catalog-client.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/execution/local-model-executor.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/execution/kv-session.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts` (remove after migration)
- `packages/core/src/index.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/index.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/server/serve.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/router.ts`
- `package.json`

## Contracts and schemas

Proxy service config and readiness/drain state; no new workload lifecycle schema. In-flight state and disposable catalog snapshots are the only proxy-owned request state.

## Test strategy

Add packages/proxy/test/standalone.test.ts and packages/remote/test/proxy-drain.test.ts. Start proxy with no model directory/no spawn privileges, two workers and fake backends; exercise three protocols, restart/drain, cancellation and worker KV slot lease lifetime. Retain/move existing integration tests rather than deleting coverage.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. Run focused tests and required typecheck/lint plus the AGENTS.md four-repository gate (llamactl, nova, sirius-gateway, embersynth) for implementation slices. Report unavailable sibling checkouts as gaps. No production inference/credentials in hermetic CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Proxy replicas scale/restart independently; no local model directory, login or executable is needed.
- [ ] Workers own all KV slots, processes and sessions through completion/abort.
- [ ] Dependency checks enforce core pure logic; embedded and standalone outputs/errors remain equivalent.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

Remote execution opt-in; preserve public /v1 endpoints and CLI/app workflows. Workers first, then proxies; rollback selects embedded composition without core importing remote.

## Verified baseline references

Baseline: frozename/llamactl@7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb. The implementation acceptance tests listed above are planned, not claimed as implemented or passing. Reference inspection is complete in R0.

## Execution and review discipline

Task class: BOUNDARY (producer-consumer round-trip first, then independent review). Revalidate the named file fence against current main before implementation. Shared schema/proxy edits have one owner at a time. Use the focused bun:test paths above, then `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun test` in llamactl, Nova, sirius-gateway and embersynth. If Nova changes, run `bun install` in each consumer first. Expected: exit 0, zero failures/errors; record actual baseline and added assertion counts. A shell/environment failure is not a product pass. Flags and rollback below must be tested before activation; no time estimates.

Documentation review PR: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/pull/147. Completed reference review: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/128.

## Penumbra fleet execution contract

Task ID: **P4.2**. Class: **BOUNDARY**. Type: **implement_substantial**. Suggested isolated branch: `codex/ai-router-p4-2`. Dispatch status: **blocked_on_accepted_dependencies**.

Before dispatch, resolve the registered Penumbra project by verified git origin frozename/llamactl, fetch main, read AGENTS.md, and record cwd, clean status, exact base SHA and dependency implementation SHAs. The reviewed baseline is 7443403912ab3976d18bc288de3009e2c23b7afb; use current main containing accepted dependencies, not a stale forced reset. Do not touch an operator checkout. Use an isolated worktree, one task/branch and one writer per overlapping file fence. Dependency issue closure alone is insufficient: verify its accepted PR is merged or its explicit completed-research evidence. Never dispatch a blocked child, and do not enqueue all children and assume the task queue enforces GitHub dependencies.

Implement only this issue. Treat the Concrete targets, test paths and explicit sibling targets below as the file fence. Read referenced modules freely; expand the write fence only with a recorded scope change before edits. Preserve unrelated changes. No merge, deployment, live credentials, live model runs or feature activation. Keep rollout flags at their documented defaults. Prepare a focused PR after required gates; report blockers without expanding into unrelated baseline repairs.

Use a producer-consumer assertion that fails for the intended missing behavior (RED), minimal implementation (GREEN), a deliberate relevant mutation that makes it fail, restoration, and fresh focused/full gates. Record command, cwd, exit, pass/fail/skip counts, mutation/restoration proof and exact final SHA. Characterization tasks preserve known-defect reproductions separately; documentation-only R0 does not require synthetic implementation tests. Missing dependencies, fixture services or a failing mandatory gate are blockers, not PASS. BOUNDARY work needs independent adversarial review against the final SHA and assertions; the implementer's own summary is insufficient.

Return: VERDICT: PASS or FAIL; issue URL; base/final SHAs; changed-file fence proof; test and mutation evidence; compatibility/migration/flag/rollback evidence; independent review result and unresolved findings; actual PR URL. Expected artifacts are commit, PR and review_verdict. Do not declare success from exit code alone or from empty/skipped suites. No time estimates.

### Focused checks and write fence

- cwd `packages/proxy`: `bun test test/standalone.test.ts` (planned fixture: create before running; zero matches is failure)
- cwd `packages/remote`: `bun test test/proxy-drain.test.ts` (planned fixture: create before running; zero matches is failure)

Machine-readable write fences, dependency gates, focused commands and the fully resolved `task.file` payload are in [the publication manifest](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-publication.json), selected by this issue ID. Existing test paths were checked at the reviewed baseline; planned paths are explicit deliverables. Test helpers/fixtures may be added only within the corresponding test subtree. Keep generated logs out of commits.

Composition migration preflight: enumerate all imports of core/openaiProxy.ts and the moved exports before edits; attach that exact caller list to the task and add necessary caller migration paths to its recorded fence. Preserve their assertion coverage. Do not guess that package exports alone cover all consumers.

Full gates: run `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, remote/app `tsc --noEmit`, `bun test`, `zsh test/run-all.zsh`, and each sibling repository’s `bun test` from its verified root. If @nova changes, run `bun install` in every consumer first. The documentation-time llamactl baseline was not fully green; reproduce and classify failures rather than inheriting a false PASS. Disposable PostgreSQL/pgvector and real fake executables are required where this issue names them; absent services do not count as passing integration tests.

### API binding (verified, not inferred)

The registrar submits only `fleet.task_file` after binding its verified local `project_id` and authenticated creator identity, then links the returned task ID to this existing GitHub issue using `task.link_gh`. Do not set `gh_create` or create duplicate issues. Deduplicate by existing task-to-GitHub association before filing. Project IDs, seat names, credentials and worktree paths are local runtime values, deliberately absent from the public artifact. They are not unresolved publication links.

`task_class`, `task_type`, the branch and dependency policy are registrar/chain metadata, not fields accepted by the strict task.file API. The registrar must apply them to the selected chain/worktree and lane before leasing. At the reviewed implementation, task.file stores branch_base only for orchestrate tasks, so a work-task payload cannot enforce its branch. Resolve registered seats at dispatch, preserve configured model/cost policy and require an independent reviewer; no invented seat or premium fallback is supplied. This publication prepares tasks; it does not file or execute fleet work.

Contract evidence: [task.file schema](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/api-contract/src/tasks.ts#L96-L124), [MCP handler](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/mcp/src/tools/task-file.ts#L1-L18), [writer branch semantics](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/core/src/tasks/writer.ts#L355-L390), [chain metadata](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/api-contract/src/chains.ts#L160-L186), [task classes](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/api-contract/src/lanes.ts#L1-L4), [task types](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/api-contract/src/agent-performance.ts#L3-L13), [existing-issue link](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/mcp/src/tools/task-link-gh.ts#L6-L23).

## Tracking ledger

[Initiative registrar and ledger](https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/unified-ai-router-registrar.md#work-package-ledger). Stable ID: **P4.2**; Penumbra registrar: `2c2a7cbb-048c-45e5-8663-f15187b9e85b`; phase 6; owed follow-up event **1702**. Record task/owner, actual PR/SHA, test/review evidence, migration and rollout state when work occurs. Preserve this ID and append corrections; never infer completion from issue closure alone. Current snapshot: **blocked**, no implementation task dispatched.

## Problem

A stateless proxy tier cannot rely on another proxy's SQLite file for correctness or availability. Fleet cache storage needs a service boundary and durable payload ownership while embedded exact-only mode remains supported.

3. Separate model equivalence/revision from process restart incarnation and cache generation. Never infer provider equivalence from matching model labels.
4. Define stale/duplicate/out-of-order update handling, bounded last-known-good routing and coordinator partition behavior. Session claims/revocations fail closed without valid authority.

3. Separate model equivalence/revision from process restart incarnation and cache generation. Never infer provider equivalence from matching model labels.

Add packages/remote/test/coordination-partition.test.ts; extend peer-snapshot-poller and fleet suites. Test competing owners, stale leases, database-time expiry, reordered snapshots, split views, model swap during generation, revoked owners and crash recovery.

## Problem

Model-only hashing creates hotspots, while hashing prompt bytes destroys semantic affinity. Execution placement and exact/semantic cache ownership must be distinct decisions over the same authorized route identity.

## Scope

1. Implement deterministic weighted rendezvous over authorized, capable, healthy, non-draining equivalent execution deployments. Key stateless work by scoped request affinity; bind sessions to owner. Add bounded-load admission/fallback without evading shared account quotas.
2. Route exact cache by scoped canonical request key to stable virtual shards. Route semantic lookup by compatibility namespace to the same index for paraphrases; do not hash prompt bytes for semantic ownership.
3. Use published map version/fences; allow bounded pre-acceptance stateless failover and one stale-map refresh. Never retry CLI/ACP or any request with unknown acceptance/output; prevent forwarding loops.
4. Add shared credential-account reservation/accounting across proxy replicas and route explanation/status via remote tRPC and CLI dispatcher.

[AI router P5.2] Add rendezvous execution routing and distinct exact/semantic cache affinity

## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 5 — Fleet
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/142, https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/140, https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/141.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

Model-only hashing creates hotspots, while hashing prompt bytes destroys semantic affinity. Execution placement and exact/semantic cache ownership must be distinct decisions over the same authorized route identity.

## Scope

1. Implement deterministic weighted rendezvous over authorized, capable, healthy, non-draining equivalent execution deployments. Key stateless work by scoped request affinity; bind sessions to owner. Add bounded-load admission/fallback without evading shared account quotas.
2. Route exact cache by scoped canonical request key to stable virtual shards. Route semantic lookup by compatibility namespace to the same index for paraphrases; do not hash prompt bytes for semantic ownership.
3. Use published map version/fences; allow bounded pre-acceptance stateless failover and one stale-map refresh. Never retry CLI/ACP or any request with unknown acceptance/output; prevent forwarding loops.
4. Add shared credential-account reservation/accounting across proxy replicas and route explanation/status via remote tRPC and CLI dispatcher.
5. Observe mode compares selected destinations without duplicate execution. Keep centroid/multiprobe semantic partitioning deferred until a measured hot namespace justifies recall complexity.

issues.title: [AI router P5.3] Rebalance cache shards and validate join/leave, replication and partitions
issues.body:
## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 5 — Fleet
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/143.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

Changing a cache owner is not equivalent to replicating its data. The fleet needs explicit logical ownership transfer over durable storage pools and controlled behavior during partial copies, model swaps and failures.

## Scope

1. Implement transfer states plan→copy→catch-up→drain→fenced cutover→retire with a durable cursor/outbox, idempotent writes, versioned ownership and bounded dual-read window.
2. Distinguish stateless cache-service replica failover over the same PG pool from copying a shard between pools. Use PG HA replication for storage durability; do not claim snapshots/tunnels replicate databases.
3. Preserve strict scope, original TTL, invalidation generation and payload/vector atomicity throughout transfer. Expired/revoked entries never become live at a new owner.
4. Document drain/capacity/replication-lag gates, partial-transfer resume/abort, old-owner fencing, last-known-good map bounds and rollback that freezes movement.
5. Expose shard status, transfer progress and rejected stale writes without high-cardinality metrics or secret data.

## Concrete file/module targets

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

- `packages/remote/src/cache/rebalance.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/coordination/shard-map.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/coordination/leases.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/cache/maintenance.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/cache/client.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/cache/pgvector-store.ts`
- `packages/core/src/routing/shards.ts`

## Contracts and schemas

Transfer state/cursor/outbox, storagePoolId, owner term, dual-read expiry and schema generation. Replication/copy operations preserve origin provenance and absolute expiry.

## Test strategy

Add packages/remote/test/cache-rebalance.test.ts; extend coordination-partition.test.ts and proxy-fleet-routing.test.ts. At least two proxies/three workers/cache instances with fault injection: join/leave, interrupted copy, duplicate batches, cutover crash, lagging replica, old owner writes, model swap, expiry mid-transfer and coordinator loss.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. Run focused tests and required typecheck/lint plus the AGENTS.md four-repository gate (llamactl, nova, sirius-gateway, embersynth) for implementation slices. Report unavailable sibling checkouts as gaps. No production inference/credentials in hermetic CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every failure point either resumes transfer or serves/bypasses safely without exposing stale/cross-scope payloads.
- [ ] Fenced old owners cannot write after cutover; byte-distinct semantic requests retain index affinity.
- [ ] Operational runbook defines PG HA responsibilities, lag gates and rollback; no unverified exactly-once claim.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

Enable movement only after observe and stable rendezvous gates. Rollback freezes transfers and uses a valid stable map; never remove revision fencing to regain availability.
