## Problem

Changing a cache owner is not equivalent to replicating its data. The fleet needs explicit logical ownership transfer over durable storage pools and controlled behavior during partial copies, model swaps and failures.

## Scope

1. Implement transfer states plan→copy→catch-up→drain→fenced cutover→retire with a durable cursor/outbox, idempotent writes, versioned ownership and bounded dual-read window.
2. Distinguish stateless cache-service replica failover over the same PG pool from copying a shard between pools. Use PG HA replication for storage durability; do not claim snapshots/tunnels replicate databases.

issues.title: [AI router P6.1] Add worker-owned ACP v1 ephemeral inference and protocol translation
issues.body:
## Roadmap and dependencies

Parent: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/127
Phase: 6 — ACP
Depends on: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/128, https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/135, https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/issues/140.
Design: https://github.com/frozename/llamactl/blob/docs/unified-ai-router-roadmap/docs/specs/2026-09-23-unified-ai-router-architecture.md

## Problem

ACP has no first-class llamactl implementation at the reviewed baseline. Introduce an ACP client adapter on execution workers using the official protocol and verified Penumbra patterns, without treating agent-owned tools as caller-owned OpenAI tool calls.

## Scope

1. Pin official ACP SDK/schema and selected real agent versions; incorporate R0's Penumbra reuse matrix. Implement stdio JSON-RPC initialize/capability negotiation, explicit authentication, session/new, prompt, session/update and cancel; do not assume draft HTTP transport is production-stable.
2. Expose an ephemeral text-only compatibility profile through the shared executor and all three public codecs. Define accepted history/system semantics explicitly; reject unsupported role/tool/multimodal features before spawning rather than silently flattening them.
3. Map agent text updates incrementally, terminal stop reasons and cancellation/errors to common events. Keep agent tool lifecycle as metadata; do not emit caller tool_calls for work already executed by the agent. Unknown usage stays unknown.
4. Add bounded connection/process/session pools, frame sizes, queues, timeouts and idle retirement. Reject late updates after termination; cancellation resolves pending permissions as cancelled and cleans up subprocess resources.
5. Deny interactive permission requests in ordinary inference mode. Worker execution profiles own login, environment and sandboxed workspace; declining filesystem capabilities alone is not OS isolation.

## Concrete file/module targets

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

- `packages/core/src/inference/acp-policy.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/acp/adapter.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/acp/connection.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/acp/pool.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/acp/translate-events.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/acp/permissions.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/acp/workspace.ts` (new)
- `packages/remote/src/config/provider-nodes.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/providers/factory.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/inference/procedures.ts`
- `packages/remote/src/execution/admission.ts`

## Contracts and schemas

AcpBindingSchema, pinned capability/profile and protocol versions, owner, workspace/permission policy, terminal outcome. Keep SDK implementation types remote; pure policy contracts core.

## Test strategy

Add packages/remote/test/acp-adapter.test.ts, acp-permissions.test.ts and proxy-acp.test.ts. Real fake ACP executable speaks JSON-RPC; cover init/auth/version failure, malformed/oversized frames, fragmented Unicode, interleaved sessions, unsupported features before spawn, tool denial, cancel/late updates, process death, no duplicate tools and three-protocol JSON/SSE. Add opt-in smoke tests for pinned real agents.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. Run focused tests and required typecheck/lint plus the AGENTS.md four-repository gate (llamactl, nova, sirius-gateway, embersynth) for implementation slices. Report unavailable sibling checkouts as gaps. No production inference/credentials in hermetic CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ephemeral ACP text is reachable by model from Chat, Responses and Messages clients with bounded streaming/cancel.
- [ ] No permission auto-allow, public executable/cwd override or agent-to-client double tool execution.
- [ ] Selected real agents pass the advertised capability profile; no cache or automatic retry.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

LLAMACTL_PROXY_ACP=off|ephemeral|sessions defaults off. Enable per vetted binding/profile after reference and sandbox review; ephemeral can ship before fleet stateful sessions.

The pool is a host-owned library pool instance; reuse is disabled unless the binding sets `pool: scoped`. Neither file implements framing, spawning, signalling or eviction.
5. **Permissions** (`packages/remote/src/acp/permissions.ts` (new)). The host decision function passed to the library permission context. Every `session/request_permission` gets a reject option, or is cancelled if none is offered. Trust-all is never set. Cancellation resolves pending requests as cancelled. Every decision is journaled.
6. **Workspace** (`packages/remote/src/acp/workspace.ts` (new)). A private per-request directory under a root the binding declares, removed after the terminal event. There is no caller override of executable, argv, cwd or environment. This separates workspaces; it makes no OS sandbox claim.
7. **Translation** (`packages/remote/src/acp/translate-events.ts` (new)). Maps `session/update` to P4.1 execution events. Agent message text becomes incremental deltas in order; tool calls, plans and thoughts go to operator progress only; the `session/prompt` stop reason becomes exactly one terminal; late updates are dropped and counted. Usage stays unknown unless per-request token counts are reported; context occupancy or cost is never converted into usage.
8. **Adapter** (`packages/remote/src/acp/adapter.ts` (new)). A lazily loaded provider for ACP nodes. Order: eligibility, ownership check, admission, spawn and bootstrap, model selection, prompt, bounded stream, terminal validation, then cleanup of the session, process group, workspace and admission slot.
9. **Factory** (`packages/remote/src/providers/factory.ts`). Route `source: "acp"` nodes to the adapter through a dynamic import. A process that is not the declaring agent uses the P2.1 owner dispatch over the worker RPC and never spawns locally.
10. **Worker RPC** (`packages/remote/src/inference/procedures.ts`, created by dependency P4.1). Replace the ACP typed refusal with adapter dispatch for enabled, validated bindings. Only the declaring worker publishes the ACP target in the P4.1 catalog, after binding validation (digest, conformance, selector). Add no new procedure, route or listener; P4.1 acceptance, status, cancel and unknown-outcome semantics stay unchanged.
11. **Admission** (`packages/remote/src/execution/admission.ts`, created by dependency P2.2). ACP processes count against the same worker-local admission, credential scope and drain. Edit this file only if the accepted P2.2 API cannot express an ACP process.

### Non-goals

- **Penumbra.** No full Penumbra suite dependency, and no use of Penumbra's daemon, database, workflows, memory, registrar or configuration.
- **Library channel and imports.** No private sibling source imports, and no `file:`, `workspace:`, `link:` or sibling-checkout channel. No new dependency in any package manifest.
- **Gateway and cache.** No public gateway or protocol ingress work, which is the Sirius slice. No final-response cache work: ACP results are never read from or written to the embedded exact cache or any response cache.
- **Second RPC; takeover.** No second RPC. No automatic takeover or fallback between runtimes (see Rollout). No retry after uncertain acceptance or output.
- **Sessions.** No persistent sessions, `session/load`, `session/resume`, reusable session IDs or session fencing. These belong to P6.2.
- **Reimplementation.** None of the five primitives, and no alternative ACP client.
- **Agent capabilities.** No client filesystem or terminal capability, no MCP servers passed to agents, no OS sandbox claim and no ACP HTTP transport.
- **Other code.** No change to Nova contracts, to the CLI path beyond shared factory and schema plumbing, to the P0.2 fences or to the direct local endpoint.
- **Enablement.** No binding enablement, live credentials or real-agent runs in CI.

### Write fence

Repository `frozename/llamactl`, root-relative paths. "(new)" means the path is absent at c2a6a83c, checked with `git cat-file -e c2a6a83c:<path>`.

- `packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`: ACP binding and the `acp` provider source.
- `packages/core/src/inference/acp-policy.ts` (new): pure policy.
- `packages/remote/src/config/provider-nodes.ts`: virtual ACP nodes and lookup.
- `packages/remote/src/providers/factory.ts`: routes `acp` nodes; non-owners dispatch to the declaring worker.
- `packages/remote/src/inference/procedures.ts`: new at c2a6a83c, created by dependency P4.1 (must exist on the dispatch base). Lifts the ACP refusal for validated bindings.
- `packages/remote/src/execution/admission.ts`: new at c2a6a83c, created by dependency P2.2 (must exist on the dispatch base). Edit only if its API cannot express ACP.
- `packages/remote/src/acp/adapter.ts` (new), `packages/remote/src/acp/connection.ts` (new), `packages/remote/src/acp/pool.ts` (new), `packages/remote/src/acp/translate-events.ts` (new), `packages/remote/src/acp/permissions.ts` (new), `packages/remote/src/acp/workspace.ts` (new).
- `packages/remote/test/acp-worker-rpc.test.ts` (new): the boundary round trip. It replaces the historical public-path `proxy-acp` test.
- `packages/remote/test/acp-adapter.test.ts` (new), `packages/remote/test/acp-permissions.test.ts` (new), `packages/remote/test/acp-install.test.ts` (new).
- `packages/remote/test/acp-model-selection.test.ts` (new), `packages/remote/test/acp-pool-isolation.test.ts` (new), `packages/remote/test/fixtures/acp-agent.ts` (new); v1 fence omission fixed.

**Serialization** (one writer at a time):

- `schema.ts`, `factory.ts` and `provider-nodes.ts` are also in the P1.1 fence, and P1.1 is not an ancestor. P2.1 and P2.2 are ancestors; preflight step 2 requires both merged before dispatch.
- `admission.ts` is also in the P5.2 fence, and P5.2 is not an ancestor.
- The ACP permissions, workspace, pool and policy files, `schema.ts` and `acp-permissions.test.ts` are shared with P6.2, which is serialized after P6.1 by its dependency edge.

If another lane holds a shared file, wait for it to land and rebase.

**Excluded:**

- `packages/remote/test/proxy-acp.test.ts` (replaced).
- `packages/remote/package.json` and `bun.lock`. Adoption and version bumps belong to #135 (see Dependencies).
- `packages/remote/src/cli/`, `packages/remote/src/router.ts`, `packages/remote/src/server/serve.ts` and `packages/remote/src/proxy/`.
- `packages/core/src/openaiProxy.ts` and `packages/core/src/responsecache/`.
- `packages/core/src/inference/rpc-schema.ts` (P4.1; read only).
- Every sibling repository.

Test helpers go only in the fixture file or the named test files.

### Linked repository slices

Filed just in time per follow-up 1831: only when the slice's dependencies are accepted and its payload is rebased on its repository's base. Each slice links back here. None is filed today.

- **P6.1/sirius-gateway (exposure), frozename/sirius-gateway.** Scope: catalog entries for qualified ACP profiles; public Chat Completions, Responses and Messages exposure through the P4.1 Sirius worker client; typed-unavailable propagation; no retry after output or uncertain acceptance; ACP responses are cache-ineligible. Filed when P6.1 is accepted for the profile, P1.3 is accepted and the P4.2 fail-closed exposure gate is in place.

Not slices of this package: the library qualification (P2.2/penumbra-qualification, follow-up 1830), the optional Penumbra agent-serving profile, and any Nova change. If ExecutionEventV1 as accepted in P4.1 cannot carry what P6.1 needs, stop and raise a Nova slice under follow-up 1831; never define a parallel event.

### Contracts and schemas

- **ACP binding** (`packages/core/src/config/schema.ts`) on agent nodes. Field names are proposals; defaults and required fields are the contract.

  | Field | Contract |
  | --- | --- |
  | `name` | Same rule as CLI bindings |
  | `command`, `args` | Absolute, operator-owned executable with fixed args |
  | `executableDigest` | Required unless mode is off |
  | `protocolVersion` | ACP v1 |
  | `mode` | `off` or `ephemeral`; default `off` |
  | `pool` | `disabled` or `scoped`; default `disabled` |
  | `advertisedModels`, `defaultModel` | Models the binding may serve |
  | `modelSelector` | `config_option`, or `legacy` with a pinned conformance reference for the exact digest |
  | `conformance` | Pinned conformance reference for the exact digest (see X6) |
  | `env` | Secret references resolved by the existing resolver |
  | `loginHome` | The agent's own login directory, explicit |
  | `workspaceRoot` | Root for per-request workspaces |
  | `limits` | Timeout, cancel grace, watchdog, line bytes, pending requests, queued updates, output bytes |
  | `subscription` | Journal attribution |

  `ProviderBindingSchema.source` gains `acp`. Synthesized nodes are never persisted.
- **Pure policy** (`packages/core/src/inference/acp-policy.ts`): eligibility, the model-selection verdict, pool-key inputs and the default-deny permission policy. The terminal outcome is one of `completed`, `length`, `refused`, `cancelled`, `truncated`, `incomplete` or `error`, and carries the ACP stop reason or an error class.
- **Consumed unchanged:** P4.1 InferenceRpcV1 and acceptance fencing (`packages/core/src/inference/rpc-schema.ts`); ExecutionEventV1 from the P4.1 Nova slice; the P0.2 invocation-context, usage-observation and stream-completion contracts (Nova contracts 0.2.0 from nova#1); the P2.2 admission API; the library API at the version adopted on main.
- **Terminal mapping:**

  | Source | Terminal |
  | --- | --- |
  | `end_turn` | completed |
  | `max_tokens` | length |
  | `max_turn_requests` | non-retryable error |
  | `refusal` | refused |
  | `cancelled` | cancelled |
  | Transport close or exit before the `session/prompt` response | incomplete, never completed |
  | Output cap | truncated, after `session/cancel` |

- **Pool key:** binding name, executable digest, args, protocol version, model selector, workspace policy, the tenant/account scope from the invocation context, and a credential-scope digest over the credential references, a fingerprint of their resolved values (never the values) and the login home.
- **Journal.** Tool activity, permission decisions, the stop reason, executable digest, library and protocol versions, and the selected model go to the worker journal, not to caller-visible events.

### Test strategy

**BOUNDARY test first.** Before any production edit, write `packages/remote/test/acp-worker-rpc.test.ts` with `packages/remote/test/fixtures/acp-agent.ts`.

- **Producer:** a real P4.1 worker RPC request that targets `<agent>.<acp-name>` on a worker whose configuration declares an enabled binding that runs the fixture.
- **Consumer:** every frame the P4.1 client receives is parsed with the accepted InferenceRpcV1/ExecutionEventV1 schemas. No ad hoc shape checks.

The test asserts:

1. The first text delta arrives while the fixture still holds its final `session/prompt` response. The fixture releases that response only after the test acknowledges the delta.
2. Exactly one terminal event arrives: `completed`, from `end_turn`.
3. The reported model equals the value the fixture acknowledged via `session/set_config_option`.
4. Usage is unknown, not zero.
5. A fixture tool call appears only in the operator journal, never as a caller tool call.
6. After the terminal event, the process group is gone, the workspace is removed and admission is released.
7. A second identical request reaches the fixture again, and no response-cache entry exists.

Work in this order:

1. **RED.** On the dispatch base the `acp` key is stripped, so the P4.1 catalog has no deployment for `<agent>.<acp-name>` and the catalog lookup or submit gets a typed rejection; assertion 1 fails on it. Record the exact rejection code and confirm it is not a compile or import error: the RED test imports only base modules plus the fixture.
2. **GREEN.** Write the minimal implementation.
3. **Mutation.** Make translation buffer deltas until the terminal event, and separately treat exit without a prompt response as completed. Each mutation must fail a named assertion. Then restore the code.

**Fake ACP agent** (`packages/remote/test/fixtures/acp-agent.ts`). A real executable that the library spawns (`Bun.spawn` is never mocked), speaking newline-delimited JSON-RPC ACP v1 and recording every request it receives. Scripted modes: normal; hold the final response until released; auth required; version mismatch; configOptions with and without a model selector; ignore or reject `set_config_option`; malformed frame; oversized line; UTF-8 split across writes; update flood; tool call plus permission request; die mid-stream; exit without a response; late update; dump the environment to a file; spawn a sleeping grandchild.

**Other suites** use bun:test and temp runtimes (`makeTempRuntime`/`envForTemp` or the remote helpers), `makeCluster` where a worker is needed, random ports and no live credentials.

- `packages/remote/test/acp-adapter.test.ts`: init, auth and version failures; malformed and oversized frames; fragmented Unicode; unsupported features rejected with spawn count 0; process death; late updates; a bounded queue while the consumer is paused; the output cap producing truncated; cancel before spawn and mid-stream; local compatibility via `providerForNode` with no local cache entry.
- `packages/remote/test/acp-permissions.test.ts`: every request is rejected or cancelled and trust-all is never set; pending requests are cancelled on abort; capabilities are declined and the MCP server list is empty; client tools are rejected before spawn.
- `packages/remote/test/acp-model-selection.test.ts`: an advertised selector is acknowledged; an unacknowledged or mismatched selection is refused before the prompt; a model outside the binding is refused before spawn; a legacy selector works only with a pinned conformance reference that matches the digest; the reported model is the acknowledged one.
- `packages/remote/test/acp-pool-isolation.test.ts`: pooling is disabled by default; with `pool: scoped`, any change of scope, credential digest, workspace policy, executable digest or selector prevents reuse; a sentinel secret in the worker environment is absent from the child; pools are instance-scoped.
- `packages/remote/test/acp-install.test.ts`: INSTALL-6 I1–I5, plus the testable part of I6.
- Regression: the existing `cli-adapter`, `cli-stream`, `cli-schema` and `cli-synthesis` suites stay green unchanged.
- Opt-in real-agent qualification runs behind an explicit test environment variable, is skipped by default, reports a skip as skipped (never a pass) and is not a gate.

### Acceptance criteria

EXEC-7 (applicable: X1–X6):

- [ ] **X1 model selection:** a model outside the binding is refused before spawn. With an advertised selector, `session/set_config_option` must acknowledge the requested value before any prompt, otherwise the request gets a typed refusal. Without one, execution is allowed only under a pinned legacy conformance for the exact digest. The reported model is the acknowledged value.
- [ ] **X2 worker ownership before spawn:** before admission and spawn, the adapter checks that the executing process is the declaring agent (agent name plus the P4.1 acceptance fence/incarnation). A mismatch returns a typed refusal with spawn count 0. Non-owning processes use P2.1 owner dispatch and never spawn.
- [ ] **X3 bounded streaming and capture:** the first delta arrives before the final prompt response. Line, pending-request, queue and output limits are enforced with backpressure, and overflow ends as truncated after `session/cancel`. There is exactly one terminal event: completed requires a prompt response, and EOF or exit without one is incomplete.
- [ ] **X4 cancellation end to end:** a pre-aborted request is rejected before spawn. A client disconnect, RPC cancel or deadline sends `session/cancel`, resolves pending permissions as cancelled, drains updates until the prompt terminal or grace, terminates the process group (grandchild included), removes the workspace and releases admission. No retry after uncertain acceptance.
- [ ] **X5 credential isolation:** the child environment is composed explicitly from resolved secret references and the explicit login home. The worker environment is not inherited (sentinel test). The pool key includes the credential-scope digest. No credential value reaches logs, journals, events or other products' configuration.
- [ ] **X6 tool permissions, deny by default:** filesystem and terminal capabilities are declined and no MCP servers are passed. Every permission request is rejected or cancelled, and trust-all is never set. Client tools are rejected before spawn, and agent tool activity appears only in operator progress. `mode: ephemeral` requires a pinned conformance record showing that the agent version routes tool use through permission requests; otherwise validation refuses the binding.
- [ ] **X7 session fencing: N/A.** Sessions are ephemeral: created and closed within one request and never returned for reuse. `session/load` and `session/resume` are never sent. Persistent sessions and fencing belong to P6.2, which depends on P5.1.

INSTALL-6 (baseline from follow-up 1832): basic llamactl local serving needs the grandfathered ../nova checkout, `bun install` and `llamactl server start`, with no persistent service, required config file or credential entry.

- [ ] **I1 clean install:** in a fresh temp runtime with an empty HOME and no Penumbra checkout, `~/.penumbra`, daemon or configuration, an enabled binding to the fixture serves a request. Configurations without ACP behave as before.
- [ ] **I2 existing-config upgrade:** a stored configuration with `cli` bindings and no `acp` parses deep-equal to its parse before the change. An `acp` entry without `mode` is off. No migration step.
- [ ] **I3 optional service absent:** with no binding or `mode: off`, no ACP node is synthesized, the ACP modules and library ACP entry points are not loaded, no executable is probed, and startup and health are unchanged.
- [ ] **I4 selected integration unavailable:** a missing executable, digest mismatch, init or auth failure, or protocol mismatch returns typed unavailable for that target only. Counters on other bindings, cloud nodes and every other runtime stay 0.
- [ ] **I5 disconnect and rollback:** `mode: off` refuses new requests while in-flight streams reach a terminal or grace. Other settings are untouched, and removing the binding leaves no generated files. The reverted build still loads a configuration containing `acp`, because the base schema strips unknown keys; verify and record this.
- [ ] **I6 no new mandatory service, checkout, entry point or duplicate entry:** against the baseline, required commands, services, config fields and credential entries do not increase; every new field is optional and no environment variable becomes required. Configuration stays in the existing agent-node configuration, nothing is written to Penumbra or Sirius configuration, and no install step is added beyond `bun install`. Record the ACP-backend definition sites against the 1832 duplication baseline. Enabling a binding copies no credential value (secret references only) and reuses the agent's own login home.

SHAREDLIB-6 (mandatory):

- [ ] **L1 closure:** the runtime closure reached from `packages/remote/src/acp/` holds only llamactl modules, the adopted library, Nova and existing dependencies. It contains no Penumbra core, daemon, database, workflows, memory, registrar or configuration module; the library makes no home-directory reads; and there are no private source deep imports. Evidence: the static check plus a recorded closure listing with file, byte and dependency counts.
- [ ] **L2 packed artifact:** the library is consumed as adopted on main: a packed artifact through a versioned channel, with no `file:`, `workspace:`, `link:` or sibling path. I1 passes without a Penumbra checkout, daemon, database, memory setup or extra configuration.
- [ ] **L3 consumer parity:** the llamactl ACP suites pass against the packed artifact. The Penumbra agentchat ACP suites recorded by 1830 pass against the same version; rerun them in a verified Penumbra worktree if the version differs. Penumbra's direct adapters are unchanged.
- [ ] **L4 host injection, fail closed:** llamactl supplies the environment, executable and model selector, workspace, permission decisions, clientInfo, cancel grace, watchdog and limits. A missing host input is a typed configuration error before spawn, never a library default. Pool keys include the credential-scope digest.
- [ ] **L5 package gates:** the pinned version is a released artifact with passing Penumbra package gates and a retained license notice (1830 evidence). No library code is vendored or modified.
- [ ] **L6 single runtime owner:** as stated under Ownership, tested by the I4 counters, the X2 refusal and the absence of any cross-runtime fallback path; no duplicate tool execution between runtimes (round-trip assertion 5 and X6: agent tools never surface as caller tool calls).

Package-specific:

- [ ] ACP executes only through the P4.1 worker RPC and the local provider factory. No new procedure, route or listener is added.
- [ ] The static allowlist check passes: under `packages/remote/src/acp/` and in `packages/core/src/inference/acp-policy.ts` there are 0 imports of any `@penumbra/*` package, 0 `penumbra/packages/` paths and 0 sibling source paths, except the qualified library imported under exactly the name (`LIB`) and version recorded at preflight step 3, and no framing, spawning or signalling (`child_process`, `readline`, `Bun.spawn`, `Content-Length`, `process.kill`).
- [ ] Every enabled test binding records its executable digest, ACP protocol version, library version and conformance reference.
- [ ] Gates are green against the recorded baseline, and the independent review passes on the final SHA.

### Rollout and rollback

- **Controls.** Per-binding `mode` (`off` or `ephemeral`, default `off`) and `pool` (`disabled` or `scoped`, default `disabled`), set in the existing agent-node configuration. These managed-profile settings replace the historical `LLAMACTL_PROXY_ACP` environment flag, which is not introduced. No binding is enabled here.
- **Enablement** (outside this package's authority): an operator sets `mode: ephemeral` on a vetted binding with a pinned digest and conformance record, after reference and sandbox review.
- **Disable.** `mode: off` refuses new requests with typed unavailable. In-flight streams drain to a terminal event or grace, then release their resources.
- **Code rollback.** Revert the PR; `acp` is stripped again, configurations still load, and ACP targets get a typed rejection. Record whether a config-writing command of the reverted build drops `acp`; if one does, document a backup step.
- **No automatic takeover.** A disabled, failed or refused ACP target never falls back to a CLI binding, another ACP binding, a cloud provider, Sirius or Penumbra.
- **Public exposure** stays off until the Sirius exposure slice passes its own gates.

### Fleet execution contract v2

- **Task class and type.** `task_class` BOUNDARY; `task_type` implement_substantial.
- **Repository.** `frozename/llamactl`. Verify it with `git remote get-url origin` before any write. Work in an isolated worktree, never an operator checkout. Use one branch and one writer per overlapping fence.
- **Branch.** `feat/ai-router-p6-1-acp-host`.
- **Base.** llamactl main after P0.2 acceptance, with accepted P4.1, P2.1 and P2.2 merged (reviewed at c2a6a83c). Record the base SHA and the dependency implementation SHAs.
- **Preflight.** Stop and report the blocker if any step fails.
  1. Verify origin, fetch main and read AGENTS.md. Record the cwd, clean status and base SHA.
  2. Confirm R0 (#128) is completed research and P2.2 (#135) is accepted with its PR merged. Confirm P2.1, P4.1 and P0.2 are merged. Issue closure alone is insufficient.
  3. Confirm follow-up 1830 closed as done with the ACP primitives qualified, and the P2.2 llamactl adoption merged (P2.2 accepted on Path A, or slice P2.2/llamactl-adoption accepted; never a Path B acceptance with qualification pending), so that `packages/remote/package.json` consumes the library through a versioned channel (no `file:`, `workspace:`, `link:` or sibling path) at a version exporting the five primitives listed under Qualification precondition. Record `LIB`, the exact adopted package specifier, and its version; the static check allows only `LIB`. If 1830 is still open, stop as blocked. If it was dropped or extraction proved too coupled, set `deferred_pending_qualification` and stop. If it is done but the adoption has not merged or main consumes an older version, stop as blocked with blocker `library_adoption_pending`; adoption merges first through #135 (see Qualification precondition). Never edit `package.json` or `bun.lock` here.
  4. Pin Nova to the nova main commit that contains merged nova#1 (contracts 0.2.0) and the merged P4.1/nova slice that defines ExecutionEventV1 (merge order per caveat 1829). Check out the grandfathered ../nova sibling at that commit, run `bun install` and record the SHA. Stop if the Nova slice has not merged.
  5. Re-verify the fence on the base: `procedures.ts`, `admission.ts`, `schema.ts`, `factory.ts` and `provider-nodes.ts` exist (if `procedures.ts` or `admission.ts` is missing, stop: the dependency is not accepted); every other fence path is absent. Re-run the CLI regression check.
  6. Confirm no open lane holds an overlapping fence (P1.1, P5.2, P6.2 or any other).
  7. Read the accepted P4.1 contract: where InferenceRpcV1 and ExecutionEventV1 live, and its operator progress channel, if any. Read the P2.2 admission API. Record where P4.1's backend-kind registration point and worker catalog advertisement are built. If publishing or dispatching ACP targets needs any file outside the write fence (including the excluded `router.ts` and `serve.ts`), stop and record a scope change before editing; never edit outside the fence.
  8. Before editing, record the baseline gate results: pass, fail and skip counts, and the names of failing tests.
- **Method.** RED, GREEN, mutations and restore as under Test strategy, then fresh focused and full gates.
- **Focused checks.** New test files are deliverables; zero matched tests is a failure.
  - cwd `packages/remote`, one command each: `bun test test/acp-worker-rpc.test.ts`; `bun test test/acp-adapter.test.ts`; `bun test test/acp-permissions.test.ts`; `bun test test/acp-model-selection.test.ts`; `bun test test/acp-pool-isolation.test.ts`; `bun test test/acp-install.test.ts`; regression on existing suites `bun test test/cli-adapter.test.ts test/cli-stream.test.ts test/cli-schema.test.ts test/cli-synthesis.test.ts`.
  - cwd repository root, static allowlist check with `LIB` set to the specifier recorded at preflight step 3; it must exit 0. Any `@penumbra/` specifier other than `LIB` or a `LIB` subpath, any `penumbra/packages/` path, bare or `node:` `child_process`/`readline`, `Bun.spawn`, `Content-Length` framing or `process.kill(` in the ACP host paths fails it, as does an unset `LIB`:

    ```sh
    set -o pipefail; test -n "$LIB" && test -f packages/remote/src/acp/connection.ts && { git grep --untracked -nE "['\"](node:)?(child_process|readline)(/[^'\"]*)?['\"]|Bun\.spawn|Content-Length|process\.kill\(|penumbra/packages/|['\"]@penumbra/" -- packages/remote/src/acp packages/core/src/inference/acp-policy.ts | grep -vE "['\"]${LIB}(/[^'\"]*)?['\"]"; test $? -eq 1; }
    ```
- **Required gates.**
  - llamactl root: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun test` and `zsh test/run-all.zsh`.
  - AGENTS.md cross-repository discipline (no Nova contract changes): `bun test` in verified worktrees of nova (the pinned commit containing merged nova#1 and the merged P4.1/nova ExecutionEventV1 slice), sirius-gateway (with the accepted P4.1 worker client slice) and embersynth.
  - The SHAREDLIB-6 and INSTALL-6 evidence above.
  - A shell or environment failure is not a pass. Classify failures against the recorded baseline.
- **Review.** An independent adversarial review against the final SHA and the assertions, by a different seat than the implementer. The implementer's summary is insufficient.
- **Return.** VERDICT: PASS or FAIL; issue URL; base and final SHAs; fence proof (`git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD` lies within the fence); RED, mutation and restoration output; gate counts against the baseline; EXEC-7, INSTALL-6 and SHAREDLIB-6 evidence; review verdict and open findings; PR URL. Artifacts: commit, PR, review_verdict. No merge, deployment, live credentials, real-agent runs or enablement.
task_file.acceptance_criteria: Satisfy the current rebased contract of issue #145: a worker-owned ephemeral ACP host behind the P4.1 worker RPC and the local provider factory, consuming only the qualified shared-library primitives adopted on main through the P2.2 llamactl adoption (P2.2 accepted on Path A, or slice P2.2/llamactl-adoption accepted; a Path B acceptance with qualification pending never suffices), otherwise blocked with library_adoption_pending, or deferred_pending_qualification if 1830 is dropped or extraction proves too coupled. The boundary round-trip test packages/remote/test/acp-worker-rpc.test.ts passes after a recorded RED and failing mutations. EXEC-7 X1-X6 hold (X7 N/A: ephemeral sessions only). INSTALL-6 I1-I6 and SHAREDLIB-6 L1-L6 evidence is recorded. ACP settings default off. The static allowlist check keyed to LIB (recorded at preflight step 3) passes: 0 imports of any @penumbra/* package, 0 penumbra/packages/ paths and 0 sibling source paths except the qualified library imported under exactly the adopted name and version, and no child_process, readline, Bun.spawn, Content-Length framing or process.kill in the ACP host paths. No full Penumbra suite dependency, private sibling import, package.json or bun.lock edit, second RPC, response-cache use, cross-runtime fallback or duplicate tool execution between runtimes. The diff lies within the write fence; any needed out-of-fence edit stops for a recorded scope change. Required gates, including nova at the pinned commit containing the merged P4.1/nova ExecutionEventV1 slice, are green against the recorded baseline, an independent review by a different seat passes on the final SHA, and the result is an explicit PASS or FAIL with evidence. No merge, deployment or feature enablement.

issues.body:
## Roadmap and dependencies

## Problem

Stateful agent sessions carry side effects, workspaces and credentials that cannot migrate like stateless requests. Resumption must be capability-gated, tenant-bound and protected against concurrent turns and stale owners.

## Scope

1. Implement opaque tenant-scoped session handles bound to worker/connection/session incarnation, owner lease/fence, expected turn and agent/config revision. Reject concurrent or replayed turns unless explicitly idempotent.
2. Support optional load/resume/close only when negotiated with the pinned agent. Suppress replayed updates from loaded history; do not claim generic transcript replay can recover side effects or migrate opaque sessions.
3. Add approved automation permission policies through the authenticated control plane, with audit records and path/symlink-safe workspace checks under an actual process sandbox. Public inference requests cannot grant themselves approval.
4. Define idle TTL, max sessions, retirement, owner loss, drain and unknown-outcome responses. On owner failure require explicit recovery or a new session; never silently reroute to a CLI fallback.
5. Add registration/doctor/status through core schema, remote tRPC and CLI dispatcher; surface capabilities/login readiness without secrets.

All paths below are repository-root relative. New paths are proposals, not claims about existing files.

## Contracts and schemas

SessionOwnerV1, expectedTurn, tenant-bound handle, permission decision/audit and session lifecycle with owner fencing. Capability-gated resume/close; no automatic durable replay guarantee.

Cover cross-tenant handle reuse, stale owner/term, concurrent turns, absent optional capabilities, load replay, pending permission cancel, workspace/symlink escape, logout/token rotation, crash during tool execution and bounded drain.

Use bun:test with makeTempRuntime/envForTemp, makeCluster, random-port fixture servers and real fake executables; do not mock Bun.spawn. - [ ] Only the authorized tenant and current fenced worker may advance a session turn.
- [ ] Owner loss and ambiguous side effects are explicit errors; no transparent replay or migration.
- [ ] Permission decisions and session cleanup are auditable; all supported resume/close behaviors are verified against pinned agents.

- **Transitive prerequisites.** P0.2, P4.1, P2.1 and P2.2 must all be accepted. Issue closure is not acceptance: verify the merged PR on main and the registrar record.

### Problem

Stateful agent sessions carry side effects, workspaces and credentials that cannot migrate the way stateless requests do. P6.1 is ephemeral only. The R0 review found process reuse with fresh sessions and no `session/load` or `session/resume` path. Without owner binding, fencing, turn sequencing, capability gating and host-controlled deny-by-default permissions, a gateway replica or a second worker could replay a turn, adopt a session after a lease change, or run a tool twice.

### Scope

1. **Handles.** Issue opaque, tenant-scoped handles bound to:
   - the P5.1 owner handle: worker ID, incarnation, and lease term or fencing token;
   - the connection and vendor-session incarnation;
   - the agent profile, pinned executable/version and agent/config revision;
   - the credential-scope digest and workspace.

   Scope comes from the server-derived principal in the P0.2 invocation context and the P4.1 service claims, never from client fields. Direct local mode scopes sessions to the local bearer principal. A foreign handle and an unknown handle return the same not-found response.

   Check order: decode the handle; if the owner reference (worker ID and incarnation) is not this worker, return `session_stale_owner` without a store lookup; look up the record within the caller's server-derived scope, and return `session_not_found` if it is absent or out of scope; if the record's runtime owner is not `llamactl-worker`, return `session_runtime_mismatch`; then check the lease term and `expectedTurn`.
2. **Turns.**
   - Every turn carries `expectedTurn` and an optional idempotency key.
   - A session has at most one turn in flight. Concurrent, replayed and out-of-order turns are rejected.
   - An idempotent retry returns the recorded terminal or `unknown_outcome`; it never re-executes.
   - A model or mode change is accepted only at an idle turn boundary, after revalidation against the pinned selector.
3. **Load, resume and close** are offered only when negotiated with the pinned agent.
   - Load suppresses historical updates from render, usage and billing.
   - Resume does not replay history.
   - An absent capability returns a typed unsupported error. If the owner restarts, the session is lost.
   - No claim that transcript replay recovers side effects or migrates sessions.
4. **Host automation permission policies** (llamactl host policies).
   - Registered and audited only through the authenticated operator control plane: tRPC and the CLI.
   - Default deny. Request fields never grant approval.
   - A bounded per-session ledger, adapted from the [R0 reference behavior](https://github.com/frozename/penumbra/blob/c264644bc2b4f1e1429e845208fd6ca7f6426d62/packages/agentchat/src/adapters/stdio-acp-permission.ts#L187-L280). It comes either through the qualified library version that P6.1 adopted or as a llamactl reimplementation; it is never deep-imported.
   - No cross-session decision replay. A timeout denies; a cancel resolves the request as cancelled; duplicate callbacks are idempotent.
   - An approved filesystem or terminal callback executes once, on the owner, under canonical path and symlink checks in the P6.1 sandbox. It never becomes a caller-owned function call.
5. **Lifecycle.**
   - Idle TTL, per-worker and per-tenant limits, retirement, drain and owner loss.
   - A crash after acceptance returns `unknown_outcome`.
   - Logout or credential rotation invalidates the session.
   - Recovery means opening a new session. Never silently reroute to a CLI fallback, another worker or another runtime.
6. **Fleet mode (opt-in).**
   - Owner records use additive migration `002` in the P5.1 store.
   - `open` commits the `SessionOwnerV1` record by compare-and-set under the current P5.1 lease term before the P6.1 host binds or spawns a connection; a failed commit spawns nothing.
   - The owner verifies its lease term with database time before each turn. The turn counter advances by compare-and-set on that term.
   - After a lease loss, the owner rejects turns and nothing adopts the session.
7. **Single worker RPC.** Session operations use a negotiated `SessionTurnV1` extension of the single P4.1 worker RPC. An unknown required feature fails closed.
8. **Operator controls.**
   - Configuration fields: session mode (default `off`), limits and policies.
   - tRPC status, doctor and policy procedures in a module mounted from the router.
   - `llamactl node` CLI verbs.
   - Status reports capabilities and login readiness without secrets.
9. **L6 guard.** Owner records carry the runtime owner `llamactl-worker`. A test proves that cross-runtime takeover is rejected.

### Non-goals

- **Penumbra independence.**
  - No full Penumbra suite dependency.
  - No private sibling `src` imports.
  - No Penumbra daemon, database, workflows, memory, registrar or configuration.
  - No `file:`, `workspace:` or sibling-checkout channel for any shared library.
- **No new infrastructure.**
  - No new ACP transport, process or pool primitives.
  - No second RPC.
  - No `package.json` or `bun.lock` change.
  - No new mandatory service; PostgreSQL is needed only for fleet mode.
- **No gateway or cache work.** No public gateway or protocol ingress, and no final-response, exact or semantic cache. Session turns are never cached.
- **No takeover, migration, transparent replay or fallback** between runtimes or workers, or to a CLI path.
- **No work owned by other packages or runtimes.**
  - No Penumbra developer approvals or run state.
  - No optional full Penumbra delegation (unfiled, decision 1828).
  - No Sirius code; that belongs to the linked slice.
  - No Nova change and no `ExecutionEventV1` definition; that belongs to P4.1's Nova slice.
  - No change to P5.1 or P5.2.
- **No live verification.** No persistent-session claim for an unqualified agent version. No live credentials or live models in hermetic CI.

### Contracts and schemas

- **`SessionHandleV1`**: an opaque, versioned routing envelope. It carries only the owner reference (worker ID and incarnation) and a random session ID of at least 128 bits. It contains no tenant, credential, workspace or vendor-session data. It is not a bearer credential: the owner re-checks the server-derived scope on every operation.
- **`SessionOwnerV1`** (llamactl domain), with these fields:
  - session ID and scope digest;
  - P5.1 owner handle (worker ID, incarnation, lease term or fencing token);
  - runtime owner `llamactl-worker`;
  - agent profile, pinned executable/version and agent/config revision;
  - credential-scope digest and connection incarnation;
  - negotiated `{load, resume, close}`;
  - `expectedTurn`;
  - state `open|busy|idle|draining|retired|lost`;
  - timestamps.
- **`SessionTurnV1`** (negotiated extension of P4.1 `InferenceRpcV1`): `{handle, op: open|turn|load|resume|close, expectedTurn, idempotencyKey?}`.
  - Results reuse the pinned Nova terminal and usage payloads and `ExecutionEventV1`, which P4.1's Nova slice defines.
  - Typed errors: `session_disabled`, `session_not_found`, `session_turn_conflict`, `session_stale_owner`, `session_owner_lost`, `session_capability_unsupported`, `session_limit`, `session_runtime_mismatch`, `permission_denied`, `unknown_outcome`.
- **`SessionPolicyV1`**: mode `off|single-node|fleet` (default `off`), idle TTL, limits, drain grace and decision timeout.
- **`AutomationPermissionPolicyV1`**: ID and revision, scope, allowed tool kinds and canonical roots, ledger bound. Default deny.
- **`PermissionDecisionAuditV1`**: decision, session, turn, tool-call ID, policy ID and revision, and outcome `allow|deny|timeout|cancelled|overflow`. No secrets.
- **Migration `002`**: an owner table keyed by session ID, with a fencing term and a compare-and-set turn counter, using database time. It has no destructive down migration.
- **Consumed, unchanged:**
  - P0.2 invocation, usage and stream-completion contracts;
  - P4.1 RPC and service claims;
  - pinned Nova payloads;
  - P5.1 leases and owner handles;
  - the P6.1 ACP host.
- **Evolution.** Changes are additive and negotiated, and no field is reused. Golden fixtures are handed to the Sirius slice. A shared shape moves to Nova only when both consumers agree, and not in this package.

### Test strategy

Use `bun:test`, `makeCluster` from `packages/remote/test/helpers.ts`, the `makeTempRuntime`/`envForTemp` pattern, random ports and real fake executables. Never mock `Bun.spawn`. Record baseline counts and failing test names first.

1. **`packages/remote/test/acp-fleet-session.test.ts` (BOUNDARY, written first).**
   - **Setup.** Two workers, P5.1 coordination on a disposable PostgreSQL, and `test/fixtures/acp-session-agent.ts`.
   - **Direction.** The producer is the owner's session host, reached through the real P4.1 worker RPC. The consumer is the P4.1 embedded client, which parses results through the real `InferenceRpcV1` and pinned Nova schemas.
   - **Assertions.**
     - Open returns a handle.
     - Turn 1 yields exactly one terminal.
     - The handle sent to the non-owner returns `session_stale_owner`, and that worker's spawn counter stays 0.
     - After a forced P5.1 term change, the old owner rejects the turn and the new holder does not adopt the session (`session_owner_lost`).
   - **RED.** Write the test against only the wire schema and the fixture, with no imports from unwritten modules. RED must be an assertion failure for the contract gap (the RPC rejects the unsupported session extension), not a compile error.
   - **Mutation.** Disable the term comparison in `sessions.ts`; the test must fail. Then restore.
2. **`packages/remote/test/acp-session-lifecycle.test.ts`.** Covers:
   - expected-turn mismatch; concurrent, replayed and out-of-order turns; idempotent retry;
   - cross-tenant handles, which get the same not-found response as unknown handles;
   - fleet-mode open ordering: when the owner-record compare-and-set commit fails, `open` returns a typed error and the spawn counter stays 0;
   - absent capabilities;
   - load replay suppression: history before current output is not rendered or billed;
   - resume without replay, and close;
   - idle TTL, limits and bounded drain;
   - a crash mid-tool, which returns `unknown_outcome`;
   - logout or rotation invalidation;
   - model/mode changes mid-turn versus at the boundary;
   - cancellation end to end.
3. **`packages/remote/test/acp-permissions.test.ts` (extends P6.1).** Covers:
   - default deny, with request-supplied approval ignored;
   - unauthenticated or inference-scoped policy registration rejected;
   - cross-session replay;
   - timeout and cancel races;
   - ledger overflow;
   - symlink escape;
   - duplicate callbacks executing once, measured by the fixture's side-effect counter;
   - audit without secrets.
4. **`packages/remote/test/acp-session-runtime-owner.test.ts` (L6).** Covers:
   - a record in the caller's scope whose runtime owner is not `llamactl-worker` returns `session_runtime_mismatch` and nothing is spawned;
   - a second worker or host instance cannot adopt a session;
   - no CLI or other-runtime fallback: the fake CLI spawn counter stays 0;
   - no duplicate tool execution after an unknown outcome;
   - no module-global session registry.
5. **`packages/remote/test/acp-session-install.test.ts`.** Fixtures for INSTALL-6 I1–I6. The CLI verb runs through a real `bun` process against a temporary runtime.
6. **`packages/remote/test/fixtures/acp-session-agent.ts`.** A real ACP stdio executable. It provides:
   - capability toggles and a version string;
   - historical replay;
   - permission requests;
   - a side-effect counter;
   - a mid-tool crash;
   - ignoring cancellation.

A missing PostgreSQL is a blocker, never a skip or a pass. No vendor login and no live model.

### Acceptance criteria

**Evidence and review:**

- [ ] The round trip is recorded RED, then GREEN, then failing under the mutation, then passing again after restoration.
- [ ] Only the authorized tenant and the current fenced owner can advance a turn.
- [ ] Owner loss and ambiguous side effects are explicit errors. There is no transparent replay, migration or re-placement.
- [ ] Permission decisions and cleanup are auditable. Supported load, resume and close are verified against the negotiated capability; unsupported ones return the typed error. Verification against pinned real agents is owed to Q-02 before any enablement and is outside this dispatch.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only <base>..<final>` stays within the write fence. There are 0 imports of any `@penumbra/*` package, 0 `penumbra/packages/` paths and 0 sibling source paths, except a qualified-library import that uses exactly the name and version P6.1 adopted.
- [ ] Required gates exit 0, with counts diffed against the baseline. Independent review passes at the final SHA.

**EXEC-7:**

- [ ] **X1 model-selection enforcement.** N/A as a new obligation: P6.1 owns it. Non-regression: the selector acknowledged at open holds for the session. Changes are accepted only at an idle boundary after revalidation; mid-turn changes are rejected.
- [ ] **X2 worker ownership before spawn.** N/A as a new obligation: there is no new spawn path, and P6.1 verifies ownership. Non-regression: a non-owner spawns nothing, and in fleet mode `open` commits the owner record before the P6.1 host binds or spawns, so a failed commit spawns nothing.
- [ ] **X3 bounded streaming and capture.** N/A as a new obligation: P6.1 and P1.3 own it. Non-regression: replayed history is discarded incrementally, the ledger and audit queue are bounded, and overflow denies.
- [ ] **X4 cancellation end to end.**
  - Cancel through the P4.1 RPC reaches the agent as `session/cancel`, pending permissions end as cancelled, and there is exactly one cancelled terminal.
  - If the cancel is not acknowledged within the grace period, the outcome is `unknown_outcome` and the session is retired.
  - Drain and rollback cancel no unrelated conversation.
- [ ] **X5 credential isolation.** Sessions are bound to a credential-scope digest, and rotation invalidates them. Pool entries are never shared across scopes, and outputs carry no secrets.
- [ ] **X6 tool permissions deny by default.** Without a policy, requests are denied. Only the operator control plane registers policies. An approved callback executes once, on the owner, within canonical roots.
- [ ] **X7 session fencing.** Each turn checks scope, owner handle, P5.1 lease term, `expectedTurn` and that only one turn is in flight. Stale, concurrent and replayed turns are rejected, and nothing adopts a session.

**INSTALL-6:**

- [ ] **I1 clean install.** Default configuration: mode `off`; no PostgreSQL, Penumbra, Sirius or new command; status reports sessions disabled.
- [ ] **I2 upgrade.** An existing configuration loads unchanged, and the ephemeral ACP, CLI and model paths are unchanged. Migration `002` runs only in fleet mode, and is idempotent and additive.
- [ ] **I3 optional service absent.** With PostgreSQL, Sirius and Penumbra absent, startup and health are unaffected.
- [ ] **I4 selected integration unavailable.** In fleet mode, a missing store or lease fails closed with typed errors. There is no fallback to single-node, a CLI path, another worker or another runtime.
- [ ] **I5 disconnect and rollback.** Mode `off` drains sessions without cancelling unrelated conversations and preserves settings, credentials and data.
- [ ] **I6 no added setup.** A diff of required commands, services, configuration fields and credential entries against the baseline shows:
  - no new mandatory service, sibling checkout or setup entry point;
  - the existing configuration file and `llamactl node` reused;
  - the ACP credential still referenced once, through P6.1;
  - `../nova` remains the grandfathered baseline (follow-up 1832).

**SHAREDLIB-6:**

- [ ] **L6.** One runtime owns each process, credential set, permission decision and session. The takeover test rejects adoption. There is no silent reroute to a CLI fallback or another runtime, no duplicate tool execution and no module-global state.
- [ ] **L1–L5 inherited from P6.1 and P2.2.** No new library dependency, channel or version. If the ledger comes from the library, it must be in the version P6.1 qualified; otherwise it is reimplemented in llamactl.

### Rollout and rollback

- **Default off.** Session mode is `off` by default, and no policy is registered, so every request is denied.
- **Enabling.** `single-node` or `fleet` may be enabled per profile only after the pinned real agent version passes the separate, operator-authorized real-agent qualification (ledger Q-02, host-specific proof per boundaries §6: model acknowledgement, cancellation, usage and negotiated load/resume/close). Fixture evidence alone never enables a profile. `fleet` without the P5.1 store fails validation closed.
- **Rollback.** Set mode `off`: no new sessions are accepted. Active turns complete, or end as `unknown_outcome` at the drain grace, and the sessions retire. Other traffic is neither cancelled nor rerouted. There is no takeover and no retry through another route. Migration data expires in place.
- **Public session reachability** through Sirius stays off until the P6.1/sirius-gateway exposure slice and the P6.2/sirius-gateway slice pass their own gates.
- **ACP caching and retries** stay disabled. This dispatch activates nothing.

decisions.D1_owner_allocation: Per boundaries §6. llamactl: infrastructure control plane, model workers, engine KV, qualified infrastructure CLI/ACP execution. Sirius: full inference gateway, protocol/provider routing, admission, final-response exact/semantic cache. Embersynth: synthetic composition, stage execution, evidence. Penumbra: developer harness and its own sessions. Nova: shared contracts and protocol adapters.
decisions.D2_coordinator_and_slices: Issues #128-#146 remain the single coordinators with stable IDs. Repository-owned implementation slices are recorded in manifest slices[] (id '<ID>/<repo-short>', parent_id, repository, scope, dependencies, dispatch_state 'not_filed', linked_issue_url null). A sibling-repository issue is filed just in time, when the slice's dependencies are accepted and its payload is rebased on that repository's base, and it links back to the coordinator. No duplicate work-package issues.
decisions.D3_dag: Option B, 24 native edges. Remove P1.3->P2.1, P2.2->P4.1, P3.3->P4.1, P4.2->P6.1, P5.2->P6.2. Add P0.2->P4.1, P4.1->P2.1, P1.3->P4.2, P3.3->P4.3, P5.1->P6.2. Each removed edge's acceptance requirement is carried by a named replacement (see dag.replacement_acceptance).
decisions.D4_p61_option_b: P6.1 is worker-side ephemeral ACP only (worker RPC plus local compatibility). Public exposure of qualified CLI/ACP profiles is a Sirius slice gated on P2.2 (CLI) or P6.1 (ACP) acceptance for that profile, P1.3, and the P4.2 fail-closed exposure gate.
decisions.D5_execution_event_definer: ExecutionEventV1 has exactly one definer: the Nova contracts slice of P4.1. P0.2 (in flight) and P1.3 must not define it; P1.3 uses P0.2 contracts until P4.1 lands.
decisions.D6_gate_bundles: INSTALL-6 applies to every rebased open package. SHAREDLIB-6 is mandatory on P2.2 and P6.1 and its single-owner gate (L6) applies to P2.1 and P6.2. EXEC-7 invariants are stated explicitly per package.
decisions.D7_shared_library: Qualify, do not assume. A Penumbra qualification slice (P2.2/penumbra-qualification) produces evidence for SHAREDLIB-6 on a packed candidate with no llamactl adoption. Adoption by llamactl happens only after every SHAREDLIB gate passes. Library home and distribution channel are chosen by the operator from the qualification evidence before adoption; file:, workspace:, git-sibling and private-src deep imports are never acceptable channels. If extraction proves too coupled: keep the existing narrow llamactl CLI path (P2.1/P2.2 proceed on it) and defer expanded ACP (P6.1 stays deferred) rather than reimplement a full ACP stack or depend on the full Penumbra suite.
decisions.D8_optional_delegation: Full Penumbra delegation (run/profile descriptors, provider-penumbra) stays optional and unfiled until a concrete harness workload exists; it is never a prerequisite of R0-P6.2 and never on the default infrastructure path.

replacement_acceptance.P1.3->P2.1: P2.1 no longer waits for gateway streaming/cache/usage. It now follows P4.1 (worker RPC with bounded streaming, cancellation and P0.2 invocation context) and must itself enforce bounded CLI output capture and physical usage provenance (X3).
replacement_acceptance.P2.2->P4.1: The worker RPC no longer waits for CLI lifecycle. P4.1 must refuse CLI/ACP targets (fail closed, typed unavailable) until the owning lifecycle package (P2.2 for CLI, P6.1 for ACP) is accepted for that profile; P4.2's exposure gate enforces the same at the gateway.
replacement_acceptance.P3.3->P4.1: Per boundaries §6 the worker RPC carries no cache semantics. The worker path must never serve approximate reuse (asserted by the P3.3 llamactl test-only slice); the cache-service dependency moves to P3.3->P4.3.
replacement_acceptance.P4.2->P6.1: P6.1 no longer needs the gateway deployment. Public reachability of ACP profiles is a Sirius slice gated on P6.1 + P1.3 + the P4.2 fail-closed exposure gate.
replacement_acceptance.P5.2->P6.2: Session fencing comes from P5.1 (leases, fencing tokens, session-owner handles); session turns route by owner handle and are never re-placed by rendezvous. P5.2 acceptance must honor P5.1 session-owner handles.

added_rationale.P0.2->P4.1: The worker RPC consumes the P0.2 invocation context, usage observation and stream-completion contracts.
added_rationale.P4.1->P2.1: Boundaries §6: thin CLI/ACP follows worker execution contracts; P2.1 implements the CLI executor behind the single P4.1 worker RPC instead of adding a second RPC.
added_rationale.P1.3->P4.2: The Sirius gateway deployment needs public incremental streaming, scoped exact cache and logical usage before it becomes the scalable tier.
added_rationale.P3.3->P4.3: The durable cache-service RPC needs the accepted exact->semantic->upstream serve gate and eviction policy.
added_rationale.P5.1->P6.2: Persistent sessions need P5.1 fencing and owner handles.
